First off. Let me say this. I enjoy the game. I do. Even if it's samey.
But Killing Floor 1 does everything better sans the movement and gun play.
The balance feels...strange? I'll go over the classes first. Then onto the other things,such as gameplay,difficulty,maps,micro transactions and other things.
The Firebug has problems killing things due to the fact that what it's class is about,burning everything,tends to take an abusrd amount of ammo to kill. But with the tier 3 weapon,the microwave gun,you shoot the floor at their feet and you kill them,but again,you don't have the ammo to actually be effective in longer waves or higher difficulties. The trench gun is trash as well. On Normal to possibly hard(with a decent support with ammo) you might be alright. But this is not a perk to take into Suicide or Hell On Earth.
The Commando. I honestly don't know what to feel about this perk class. An M14 Sharp Shooter has more ammo(if you take damage perks over ammo perks) and can stun enemies. You get to see cloaked enemies,like the Stalkers and the Patriarch. Other than that,there's no real point to this class anymore. Other classes can kill and clear minor mobs faster than you can with less ammo spent.
The Demolition perk is a funny one too. It falls into a similar problem the Firebug gets. Not enough ammo,but it's compounded by the fact that everything for this class is very expensive,and you don't get the full use out of it until at least wave 4 in longer maps. Heavy weaponry(Tier 2+3 weapons don't leave you room for a backup or a meidpistol to help your medic.) is fun,but you have to aim your shots and hope a Zed doesn't decide to spin you as you fire a rocket at a raging Scrake. There is a required perk,the one that lets your weapons resist Siren screams. But the perks feel half baked and not well thought out(I.e Less ammo for slightly more damage on a direct hit?)
The Medic. Can carry all his weapons at once without the need to carry dual 9mms. But the AR has funny recoil to me(this is subjective). The shotgun,I abseloutly love it. But it lacks ammo and stopping power compared to the Supports M1014. The SMG is pretty much pointless as it burns through ammo far too quickly to be useful(less ammo than the rifle the class gets.) and the pistol is overall a decent backup or off perk weapon for any class if you can carry it(sorry Demo!) YOu heal stuff,drop fart bombs and heal and poison. You're an essential player in harder difficulties. But if you're the last one,and you don't know what to do,you will get swamped quickly,especially with how quickly the weapons burn through ammo.
The Sharpshooter. Do the Commandos job but better! Carry an M14 if you want to be killing anything that moves. It's less powerful than any of the other weapons,and is about equal to the top tier weapon for the Commando,the SCARH. It's more accurate,and can penetrate or stun nearly any Zed you fight. Coupled with a high rate of fire,it's a stellar weapon. The Railgun is laughably overpowered if you can aim. If you can gather a group togeather you can freeze them with a grenade making easy pickings.
The Gunslinger,in KF1 was rolled into the Sharpshooter. These guns were your backups. They're all pistols. The only major downside to the Gunslinger is reload times. You have to plan ahead for this class,or risk getting swamped. This class,with Deagles,or 1911s is just as effective as a Commando at trash cleaning. The nail bomb is only effective in very small hallways.
The Support is all about the shotguns. Usually working with the Firebug and behind the Beserkers,they are all about keeping people stocked with ammo(once per wave) and killing anything that moves. A double barrel with the AA12 means you have won the game.  One of the strongest classes in the game. Even without a beserker to take the heat off,you can easily hold back the tide until you run out of shells.
The Beserker...well...I feel really bad for zerker drivers. This perk has been nerfed into the dirt. It's not useful at all as the support class can do it's job better and faster. Can't parry or block a boss or enraged Scrake or Fleshpound,so your formerly strongest abiltiy is rendered moot. Any other class with better weapons than you can do your job better than you. This class is pointless now.
Sharp Shooter,Gunslinger,Medic and Support are the main classes. The others aren't that great anymore in higher tier play,and often have problems in some way(i.e ammo,cost or weight) that hinder them more than they can help a team. If you were thinking about picking a perk,go with the 4 I mentioned if you want to play higher levels,and the others for Easy or Normal.
Now onto the maps. They're tiny,and dark for the most part. While they are well designed, I feel like they are overly cramped and the official maps number while much better than it was,still feels too few. There's tons of custom maps that range from awesome,to crap. At times, I do with that there were additional ammo spawns due to some classes needing more ammo.
Now, TWI has done some questionable things to balance the game well. Between the long times between patches,sometimes it feels like TWI doesn't do anything at all. For example,the reistances feel strange and awkward. But the gameplay itself feels solid. The graphics are great.  But the balance between classes is still in a strange place.
There is a PVP mode. It sucks. Don't bother with it.
Now,for microtransactions.
There's tons of problems with them,crates not opening,infinite loading so you can't open them,or the fact that you need to spend nearly 3$ an item to open it. There seems to be no point, If you get a crate or usb stick,I'd just sell it on the market,or not even bother.
Overall?
It's fun,but there's not much meat here. Theres no charm that makes it stand out compared to KF1. If you really want the game,get it on sale. But certainly try before you buy on a free play weekend.

In space, when you're all out of missiles, the fire from the engine room consumes the life support system, and the hull of the ship is crumbling around you, no one can hear you scream. That is, if any of your crewmates were still alive. They've been eaten by insectoids.
Game over.
FTL is a mix of roguelike-alike and chaos management, in space, aboard a fragile ship that looks remarkably like the previous n million that were sent to their doom in some horrible, regrettable fashion. You'll love it regardless - you're saving the galaxy, fighting the rebel scum, as you plot a galactic (escape) course to ultimate (unlikely) victory... you'll love it right up until it's fiery gibs explode and float off to join the growing debris of your many failures.
Depth of mechanics and instant high replayability make FTL a winner. There's no doubt lots of successful strategies, but appropriately for the genre, uncovering them is both challenging and fun. Even when you're screaming.

50 hours isn't the sum total of time I put into this game, it's probably closer to 70. I beat every challenge, finished all the DLC and got the true ending. I similarly 100%'ed the previous Rocksteady Arkham games.
Sad to say, Arkham Knight makes me happy that Rocksteady's time with the franchise is apparently at an end. It's no doubt a good game, but it doesn't innovate like the original did and instead allows the Arkham formula to stagnate. The single biggest problem is the sheer repetitive nature of Arkham-style combat. Even on hard difficulty, it's the easiest thing in the world to bounce between opponents building your combo meter. Each new game in the franchise tried to solve this problem by adding more enemy types who had to be stunned or lept over first, but all this does is make it frustrating when Batman targets the wrong goon and ends your combo through no fault of your own. This problem could be overlooked if you only had to fist fight people occasionally, but instead it's an entire third of the core game.
The stealth gameplay has improved, but as with the previous games it's still too easy to sneak around and CQC everyone.  Enemies now call out to each other and respond realistically, which is an atmospheric improvement but doesn't fix any gameplay problems. New enemy types have the ability to block or detect your detective mode vision but they're very rare and don't present any great challenge. It's all too easy by half.
Arkham Knight adds vehicle combat and it's one of the game's stronger points. It's viscerally satisfying to pop off "headshots" on enemy drones while dancing between their incoming projectiles, building a combo that (for reasons never explained in the game's logic) allows you to unlock a missile barrage. Tank combat felt unique, with its rythmic pacing and focus on dodging and positioning. It was certainly more involving and challenging than the fist fights.
The story in this game has huge problems. Where Arkham Asylum excelled by giving the player a clear, relatable goal (stop the Joker) and surrounding it with auxillary stories and challenges, Arkham Knight fails by overstuffing its core story with characters, doomsday devices and speechifying. The newly redesigned Scarecrow starts out intimidating but quickly loses all significance when he appears on Gotham's digital billboards every 30 seconds to opine lamely about the true nature of fear. He quickly becomes pathetic and unconvincing as a threat, and the same is twice as true for his pet soldier, the titular Arkham Knight. The Arkham Knight's inclusion in the game is completely pointless. There's another character who's inclusion is even more pointless, and they are sadly used to pollute most of the game's important plot beats with their inane nonsense. It's a very 'Spiderman 3' type narrative, in all the worst ways. None of the major story beats hold up to any degree of inquiry.
Why focus on the negatives if I like the game and want to recommend it? Because after 70 hours of playing Batman Arkham Knight, it's the negatives that really stick with you. The PC port wasn't an issue for me, I held 60 on max settings, except when I was speeding around Gotham at which point it'd occasionally dip to 30. What bothered me is how bored I got half-way through. Gaining XP stopped meaning anything because the upgrade tree is packed with useless fluff. Fights stopped being engaging because I'd done them all before a hundred times. Every defeated villain was just another reminder that the franchise had no enjoyable way of delivering boss fights. Arkham Knight is only a good game: it could have been so much more.
I recommend this game at a sale price. It's a huge amount of good content that I picked up for about £10 on CD Keys. You'll only get 50 hours out of it if you're a crazed completionist who needs something to do with their hands while listening to podcasts. Sadly it's just not that engaging.

Have you ever wanted to be in a sci-fi space horror movie? If so, then Dead Space is for you.
The best aspects of Dead Space are the sound, music, and overall solitary/frightening mood the game sets. There were several occasions where I found myself turning around because I heard something echoing in the distance… sounding as if it was coming closer. Even the zero gravity heavy steps you take sound fantastic with a hollowed, deep bass sound. When the environment is right and the audio is incredibly well done, you have a great setting for a game.
The biggest downside of the game was the linear story line. You get a few options of which upgrades you would like to make to your gear but really, you will only want to use 1 maybe 2 guns as some are very weak and pretty much useless. The character development is bland as well. Do not play Dead Space looking for a great story because you will not find it.
The gameplay may also feel stiff at first, even for a third person shooter but it kind of makes sense. You are in a heavy space suit, your mobility should be limited. To counter this, the gun controls are tight and precise. You can really feel the power of them (especially once upgraded).
Even with the nearly non-existent story, the environment really immersed me. Play the game, take your time going through it; do not rush it. 8.5/10

My one big con for DeadSpace: unresponsive controls.
My list of pros: The cinematic quality of the portion I've played is astounding. Nearly unparalleled. I'm almost happy to give up some control responsiveness for how gorgeous and immersive this game is. You have to play it to understand. And if you're the least bit adventurous, in the middle of the night with some nice headphones, in the dark. The jumpscares are great! I think this game made my little brain go "DIE!DIE!DIE!KILLITWITHFIRE!!!" more than any other game before it. But lemme say something again, the movement and punch/kick controls are terrible. Like I said, I'm ALMOST happy to give up some control responsiveness, too much was taken away though. But if you sharpen your aim enough, and make those couple of hits you DO have time to get in count, well, you can learn to live with it. It's certainly one of the most sluggish I've ever played.
The sound (even if at times predictably string-section-horror-y) and music fit the setting very well. And the visuals, I'm happy to say are impressive in many ways even today, in 2014. Something else worth mentioning is how expertly executed the TOTAL absence of user-interface was in DeadSpace. I absolutely LOVE that everything about the world you're in, must be accessed through the character you inhabit. He has various projectors built into his suit which project the prompts, information, and statistics you would expect to find up front and in your face with this type of game. But here, you see it as your character might, seemingly floating in the air beside your character. As you pan and position your camera angle, the world rotates in a detached way, giving you moments of surreal perspective on what you might look like from someone elses eyes in there, in that dark bloody mess of a futuristic room. The experience is certainly not one I think any mature gamers should miss. This would've INSTANTLY cursed me with nightmares for a month when I was younger.
As for the story, replayability, and evolution of the game. I actually haven't played through the entire thing and don't want to misjudge it based only on what I've seen so far between PC and console version. But either way, it has been very good over all and a game I definitely recommend picking up.

After receiving the game in the EA Humble Bundle alongside Dead Space 3, I felt almost obligated to get my money's worth and play this game. I must say, my initial reaction was not favorable at all. The mouse control had a horrible lag to it, which in a survival-horror game makes for a terrible experience, almost completely unplayable!
But I was not discouraged, after doing some research I found that there was an easy fix for this problem. The solution varies based on your graphics card. Because I run dual NVidia cards, I was able to use the preinstalled NVidia control to manually override the game's VSYNC settings with that of my graphics cards’. The result was a much better mouse control and playing experience! If you do not have an NVidia I strongly recommend you to find the solution that fits your graphics card.
Unto the game itself. Dead Space is spot on at creating a tense atmosphere that is completely capable of sucking you in and manipulating your emotions! While the game weighs heavily on "jump scares", it does not lack elsewhere. The environment is extremely ominous and will make you afraid to proceed to the next level!
I am not a big fan of the game's characters. The main protagonist, Isaac Clarke, is the ever clichéd silent protagonist. While it might be done to fit the tense environment, it does not make for a very lovable character and does not build a very good bond with the protagonist. Without disclaiming spoilers, the other characters of the game’s personalities are quite bland as well. I’m just going to say in the end I really didn’t give a damn what happened to them.
Aside from this, the game was quite enjoyable. I was constantly immersed in the game’s atmosphere and always taking those extra precautions steps that let you know you’re playing a good horror game! I also quite enjoyed the zero gravity rooms as well as the vacuums! They both added wonderfully to the game’s overall playability. Definitely recommend for those who want to challenge themselves and want to test their emotional capabilities! Don’t be a ♥♥♥♥♥ ;)!

FTL is a very rewarding strategy game that's easy to pick up (games only last 15-90 minutes). Permadeath truly makes you think about your decisions, and you learn much with each playthrough.
The micromanagement of crew and ship systems is well balanced and very fun. You're constantly switching power between various systems, targetting different portions of the enemy ship, and managing repairs on your own ship. It may sound dull to have to manage so much at the same time, but you quickly get the hang of it, and it's very rewarding to see your strategies work and watch the enemy ships disintegrate before you.
The other big draw is the randomization (it's a roguelike, after all). Even if you fail to beat the game, you can end up with very memorable playthroughs. It helps to inject a bit of imagination to give your crew personality, such that seeing them die or succeed will mean more to you. Playing with friends—even though it's a single player game—can really help with that.
In short, FTL is fun, has a good depth of strategy, and has a good potential for memorable experiences. I don't usually take to strategy games, but this one isn't worth passing over.

Dead Space: Succeeds where many other survival horror games fail. This game is brutal, bloody, and as hard as asteroid debris.
Pros:
+ Gore. You get a sense of dread in your stomach watching severed body segments float in zero gravity.
+ Challenging. You will die several times. Several times. You really have to want to beat this game to get to the end.
+ Long. It took me more than 17 hours to get through this game on medium, and that's pretty impressive for a game of this type.
+ Stage design is immaculate. Your objectives in each section are varied, tie in nicely with the story, and the game looks great on a nice rig.
+ The “Ripper” weapon is pure, unbridled joy.
Cons:
- The load screen makes you wait. If you try to minimize the screen and go do something else, it will still make you wait when you pull it back up. At least a third of the time you play this game you will be staring at the load screen. Ah, so this is how they meant to artificially extend playtime.
- Frustrating controls and camera angles. Why must I watch from his shoulder like a parrot? Oh, you didn't mean to hit that button? Sucks to be you. Hope you like staring at load screens.
- The protagonist is mute. When he gets ripped to shreds by Necromorphs, it's gross, but I feel no sense of connection to the hero.
- The asteroid-shooting mini-game is pure tedium.
Pro/Cons:
+/- The upgrade system is appreciated, but the changes you make to your gear don't always seem that significant.
+/- There is no cooperative mode, but then being the only person accomplishing tasks ramps up the tension.
+/- Objectives can be vague and will make you consult online guides, but then, this game doesn't always hold your hand. The stages aren't as linear as they are in the 2nd and 3rd installments, where you're carted along one path like a theme park ride.
Summary: This game is more than just Resident Evil in space. “Dead Space” does survival horror better. There is just a perfect amount of ammunition and supplies to keep you on the edge of your seat, amazing sequences, machines, and scenery, and it doesn't blatantly coddle the player. It qualifies as a classic.
Who should buy this game:
*Mature gamers that want a real survival horror challenge.
*Horror aficionados who feel that most games aren't gory enough.
Who should avoid this game:
*Gamers who want something to play with friends.
*Squeamish people that are upset by monstrous sounds, blood, and dead bodies.
I give it an 8.9 out of 10.

It's a good day when licensor titles actually have input from the creators. I was wary of this one for some time because usually licensor titles have huge flaws, but luckily this one's are minimal: The options are terrible, you can't rebind keys or do other basic functions you'd expect on a PC game. The whole feel is of a lame console port. The controls are a bit confusing since the console version relied on sticks, which keyboard/mouse users don't have. Some of the companions are embarrassingly weak, while Kyle is downright overpowered in almost all situations.
But with the bad out of the way, it's a pretty good game. Naturally it requires that you've seen a lot of South Park to know 90% of what's going on, but it has the feel of a playable South Park episode. It has a script written by Parker and Stone, it's filled with eye-buldging moments, eye hiding moments, and WTF moments that you'd expect from South Park.  Think of it as a DVD with lost episodes, only they're playable...and they kind of resemble the three-part episode they did around Black Friday 2013.
But don't expect a lot of replay value out of it. After the collectibles, that's pretty much it.

- The load screen makes you wait. If you try to minimize the screen and go do something else, it will still make you wait when you pull it back up. At least a third of the time you play this game you will be staring at the load screen. Ah, so this is how they meant to artificially extend playtime.
- Frustrating controls and camera angles. Why must I watch from his shoulder like a parrot? Oh, you didn't mean to hit that button? Sucks to be you. Hope you like staring at load screens.
- The protagonist is mute. When he gets ripped to shreds by Necromorphs, it's gross, but I feel no sense of connection to the hero.
- The asteroid-shooting mini-game is pure tedium.
Pro/Cons:
+/- The upgrade system is appreciated, but the changes you make to your gear don't always seem that significant.
+/- There is no cooperative mode, but then being the only person accomplishing tasks ramps up the tension.
+/- Objectives can be vague and will make you consult online guides, but then, this game doesn't always hold your hand. The stages aren't as linear as they are in the 2nd and 3rd installments, where you're carted along one path like a theme park ride.
Summary: This game is more than just Resident Evil in space. “Dead Space” does survival horror better. There is just a perfect amount of ammunition and supplies to keep you on the edge of your seat, amazing sequences, machines, and scenery, and it doesn't blatantly coddle the player. It qualifies as a classic.
Who should buy this game:
*Mature gamers that want a real survival horror challenge.
*Horror aficionados who feel that most games aren't gory enough.
Who should avoid this game:
*Gamers who want something to play with friends.
*Squeamish people that are upset by monstrous sounds, blood, and dead bodies.
I give it an 8.9 out of 10.

Dead Space is without a doubt an epic masterpiece, and I'll tell you why:
Set in outer space, this horror action shooter puts you in the role of somebody without any military background (you are and engineer) who has to fight for his life as he tries to figure out what happened inside the vessel you were sent to fix up, while some unidentified hostile specimens try to gut you.
The cutscenes and dialogues are special as they introduce you to the background of the Ishimura (the vessel you are at) as intriguing you why everything's so suspenseful and uncertain, you really feel like you are alone to fight for your life in every corner you take, every door you open, and pretty much every step you take. The ambient musicl is marvelous, as well as the enigmatic and frightening fog and dark, creepy lights in every room or corridor you happen to be at. You will never know what's coming up next (ok, after some hours you might already guess that a wave of specimens is gonna spawn, but trust me, even if guessing, that doesn't takes the panic away. You have to fight them back after all), and overall this game feels like you are in the main role in a sci-fi horror movie, as everything is so atmospherical you actually believe you are Isaac Clarke, it's so inmersive and deep (I recommend playing this at night with a decent volume level btw) that as the story progresses and you begin to know facts about this strange outbreak you really want to keep playing to finally unveil the truth behind your mission, everything's surrounded with mystery even 'till the end. An Instant classic that you don't wanna miss out. Oh and don't forget to play on the highest difficulty, the game will get even better as you will appreciate your ammo and health packs to a higher degree, all this to achieve the ultimate survival experience.

Shadowrun Returns is a great game. It's NOT the end-all, be-all experience we were hoping for, (not with the limited budget, time, and crew they had at any rate) but DO NOT let than fool you; it's an enjoyable game with an extremely robust editor. I'm excited by what the community can do for this game, for the first time since I saw what the NWN series' commuity did given enough time.
The cyberware (at least with the included Dead Man's Switch campaign) is not as, shall we say, robust as the books, but it appears that could change with time.
The combat system uses a pseudo X-com: Enemy Uknown cover format (with a clear shield designating light cover, medium shield designating half cover, and a full-shield designating full cover). The terrain during combat is not destructable, although the editor can include break-away walls (and in fact a few fights included this).
The Matrix environment has a either "love it or hate it" mentality, although one addition I like is the fact that being jacked into the Matrix still runs in-between rounds of combat, meaning you better hope your Chummers can cover your meat♥♥♥♥♥while you're busy noodling around in cyberspace.
The included campaign revolved arouns 9-12 hours on average, but new content (abbeviated as UGC or User-Generated Content) is being updated and/or added every day. Unfortunately for us fans of the Genesis version, the included campaign is NOT sand-box. It's fairly linear but again modders are working on creating a more open experience.

Great game for fans of old school RPG at a great price. If you've read Neuromancer; and loved it, if you've spent countless hours playing Baldur's Gate or older Fallout titles; and couldn't tear yourself away from them, this is a game for you.
And once you're done with original campaign, quality user generated content awaits you on Steam Workshop and 3rd party sites like Shadowrun Nexus. Modders are so ambitious that they are recreating whole Shadowrun sourcebooks. So, come on, join us in the shadows, chummer.
Shadowrun Dragonfall: I know they are marketing this as merely DLC, but DLC this is not. It is a full blown, old fashioned expansion pack. Dragonfall packs a bigger campaign, set in the anarchy ridden Berlin of 2054, otherwise known as the Flux State.
HBS has listened to fans and addressed all the major issues from the original game. Saving your game anywhere? Check! More interesting companions with actual personalities and backstory? Yes, sir! Side missions? Of course! This time around you are not led by the hand. You get a hub, certain Berlin neighborhood, where you can choose your missions, even reject them if Mr. Johnson offering it isn't on the level. You can chat with the (meta)humans living there. Solve their problems. Learn of their past, and they all have some very shady skeletons in the closet. Let's face it, only people running from something come to the F-State...and corporations. But the latter are a different story altogether.
Runs themselves have been improved considerably. There are multiple solutions to every problem and some tough choices to be made in practically every one. Enemy encounters have been improved. Combat is more enjoyable, overall. Non-combat skills feature more prominently. Skills and etiquette checks are very frequent. You can go in guns, fists, blades and magic blazing. But you can also do things covertly. It's all up to you.
Writing in this game is great. Story takes hold of you, is full of twist and turns, and won't let you go 'till the end. By that time, you'll crave more. Speaking of length, you'll get at least twenty hours out of the game. Even more, if you play on harder difficulties, want to speak to everyone and see everything.
Dragonfall is the definitive reason to pick up the original game. If you're into old school RPGs, cyberpunk, and value a good story, you won't be disappointed with this game.

I'm going to refrain from using the word "roguelike" for the rest of this review, because when people use that word they often really mean "procedurally generated game".
The ideal PGG is not about killing the player repeatedly (which, by the way, is not fun and never will be), but rather about providing an unlimited array of experience, an infinite variety of challenges that a sufficiently skilled and clever player can consistently surmount or excel in, and enjoy doing so. Risk of Rain is absolutely the closest thing I've ever seen to that ideal.

If you're a Shadowrun fan from old; this game is for you!  If you just like tactical rpgs or cyberpunk style games I also recommend this game. If you like any of those things, then you will enjoy this game.

Is this a true South Park game or is it just another lazy cashgrab that ♥♥♥♥♥ all over the license? First, you design your own South Park character (who happens to me mute). Right away you'll see that there's not a lot of customization options but as you progress through the game, you'll unlock new makeup, wigs and glasses that'll change your look completely. You'll also unlock new clothing gear that also provides stat boost or abilities (like a typical RPG game) and you can go to a plastic surgery clinic if you want to change the look of your character completely or look like David Hasselhoff. As soon as you meet Cartman, you have to name your character although you'll be known as either New Kid or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Make friends with everyone in South Park and add them as a friend on Facebook to unlock new perks. You also have four classes to choose from; Fighter, Mage, Thief and "Jew". I chose Jew because I had no idea what a Jew class was and I still have no idea because class system in this game is obsolete. Weapons and armour aren't limited by class so a mage can be a fighter etc.. You have a melee weapon and a range weapon at your disposal and you can equip nearly every weapons and armour with one or two "strap-ons" which provide bonuses. Earn exp to upgrade abilities and during battle, you can use items and "buddy abilities" first before picking an offensive attack on the same turn in the game's turn-based combat. You can use melee attacks, range attacks, abilities (different for each classes and characters) and you also have four "magic" abilities to choose from. Some enemies are immune to certain attacks and you can also summon certain characters once a day to end battles (except boss battles) i.e. Mr. Kim, Mr. Hankey, Mr. Slave and Jesus. You can also take down enemies with environmental kills to bypass battles and you'll still gain exp. You can call Timmy for fast travel, collect Chinpokomons, buy/sell stuff, complete quests, explore the town freely and I guess that pretty much sums up the gameplay. First of all, this game is funny as hell. There are a lot of fart jokes but for every bad joke there's always a good one and some provide contexts for those who are unfamiliar with the source material. If you're easily offended though, this game isn't for you. South Park is known for its' disgusting and crude humour and this game makes no exception. There are jokes about homosexuality, racism, abortion, pedophilia, you name it, South Park doesn't hold back. This game recreates the town of South Park so well that it's indistinguishable from the show. The aesthetics remains faithful to the show and never has a game looked like it before. The game is locked at 30 FPS so that it emulates the show (which runs at 24 FPS) and it's a wise design decision so don't be put off by it. I know PC gamers care about numbers but there's not a lot going on in this game that requires the game to run at 60 FPS so 30 is perfectly fine. Because of that, the way the characters move is also indistinguishable and your own South Park character also feels like a part of the show. You'll also have a companion to accompany you during your journey and battles; Butters, Kenny, Stan, Jimmy, Kyle and Cartman (only one companion at a time though and you can switch between characters at anytime after unlocking them). As a new kid, you moved to South Park and your parents encourages you to make friends. That's when you meet Butters who introduces you to the rest of the KKK (Kupa Keep Kids) as they all play an epic role-playing fantasy war involving humans, wizards and elves who are fighting to control the Stick of Truth (those who have the stick are all-powerful). You quickly make friends in this game and you get regular messages and status updates as well. Some are hilarous so I was a bit disappointed when you can't "like" one of the statuses and ♥♥♥♥ you Al Gore for spamming me. I like how the game uses everyday and household objects for make-believe weapons and items such as vibrators for swords, tin foil and condoms for hats, crisps for potions, used tampons for range weapons,♥♥♥♥♥♥for throwing stuff. You can also collect random (and hilarious) items (with no purpose) to sell such as ♥♥♥♥♥♥, crack pipes, pubes, Back Door ♥♥♥♥♥ 9. Things quickly become bizarre as you fight aliens, Nazi zombies, animals, hobos, fetuses, Nazi animals, Nazi fetuses, Al Gore. There's so much randomness going on in this game such as anal probing, ManBearPig,♥♥♥♥♥♥♥mouse and 16-bit Canada. And why is the shopping mall closed in the entire game? Is it to set-up DLCs? The game is a bit short so that might be it but I don't mind if that's the case as I want more of what's in the game. There are some drawbacks though. First, every characters pitches at you to hurry up during battle even though you aren't taking that long, like SHUT THE ♥♥♥♥ UP! Second, while the combat is engaging and deeper than I thought, it's also too easy. Overpowered abilities are accessible in early levels (so start with hardcore mode) but the game does allow for complex tactics from time to time such as using certain abilities/attacks against certain enemies (abilities with reduced armour effects against highly defensive enemies for example). Some of the design choices were detrimental to the game as they block prompts and objects. There are also minor glitches that causes audio, environments and characters to disappear but the biggest technical issue is the obnoxious screen tearing. There's a lack of graphical options in the game (it's 2D) but there should've been vsync and an option for button mapping. Ike and Kenny don't have their own room but that's okay because interior designs are very repetitive. I also don't see the point of morality choice, fight against Kyle or Cartman, what's up with that? This game is also disappointingly short for an RPG game. I don't mind short games as long as they have replay value so does this game have it? NO! After you complete the game, there's nothing to do. You can only fight wolves and that's it. If you haven't done any side activities, some will be available to you after you complete the game but there aren't that many so you can complete all of them quickly before you could even finish the main quests. I'm surprised that not many have mentioned these drawbacks because this game has gotten rave reviews, "Overwhelmingly Positive" on Steam. South Park has its appeal but without the license, you can see how shallow the gameplay is. I've played through this game three times so that I can get all the achievements. A lot of things are missable in this game such as friends, weapons, equipments, chinpokomons, and even side quests (which is why I said "some" earlier). It may be worth going back to pick up or do the things you've missed out on but by going back, I mean PLAYING THE ENTIRE GAME AGAIN! The only problem with playing this particular game again is that it's not as funny the second time around. I guess it's hard to laugh the second time or maybe because this game has too many fart jokes. I've only found 2 or 3 jokes that made me laugh a few times but that's it. The best thing I can say about this game is that it's a funny game that's faithful to the South Park series. Overall, this is a game is a must-own for South Park fans. Uninitiated may not understand some of the references but you'll find some laughs (assuming bad taste doesn't put you off). It's one of the most disgusting games I have ever played, but it's also really fun. As a game, it's a light RPG game but what makes this game so great is that it captures the show so authentically. This game is like an entirely new season of South Park. This is the South Park game for South Park fans, just like Hit & Run was for The Simpsons. Now I'm waiting for a Family Guy game because Back to the Multiverse sucks balls. If you're just a casual fan of South Park (like me), it's still worth playing but wait for it to go on sale. 8/10 - GREAT GAME

XCOM: Enemy Unknown is a turn-based tactical role-playing strategy game and is a reimagined remake of the 1994 cult classic strategy game UFO: Enemy Unknown (also known as X-COM: UFO Defense).
The plot centres around unknown alien forces invading Earth and through reverse engineering and battle tactics, turn the tide of the war and even drive back the alien invaders using their own weapons. While the idea behind it is grand, the execution feels a lil sloppy at times. While it does feel rather satisfying with the crowd cheering when you downed your first UFO, it never really becomes truly as epic in feel as the movie "Independence Day" The main story campaign is rather short and takes about only maybe 5 - 6 missions to complete the whole thing.
At first look, the graphics is certainly nothing to shout about and looks very 2002ish in style, with pudgy looking people and very noticeable texture pop-ins. I can't help but feel that this is probably due to the game also released for consoles and they had to dumb down the quality so consoles wouldn't explode or something. How nice it would have been had this game been a PC exclusive.
Music is by Mr Michael McCann who also scored the OST for Deus Ex Human Revolution. It definitely sounds more then a passing resemblance to that game, but that really doesn't matter as it does make me all raring up for a good fight especially when i select my soldiers and load up for the battle. This music can make going to the toilet feel like the most epic thing in the world.
The core of the game is emphasized alot on the 6 squad members where you take on missions and i must say it definitely succeeded in modernizing the style of the original game. Its really satisfying to be down to only 1 soldier and in a desperate final moment score an impossible shot complete with a zoom in "in your face" view of the kill. More then once, i fist pumped the air and squealed in delight.
Downsides, while this is a good remake and does keep to the spirit of the original, it is definitely a lighter version. While the original was truly a very in-depth strategy game where you had to manage all sorts of variables like economics and base construction to wage a successful war, this remake focus alot more on the squad combat action.
There are also alot of design ideas that don't make much sense, like being able to have 99 soldiers in the base, but only ever have 6 soldiers actually fighting. What are the other 93 of them doing in the base? Playing video games? And also only allowing 1 fighter jet to sortie against even a huge alien battleship is so rediculous. Character customization is also very limited and its unforgivable to charge money for DLCs that allows people to change the colour of their armour and hair. For shame.
Despite all those flaws however, at its core, this is a game that is worthy of the XCOM name as it definitely has the spirit of the original. It is definitely a different game then the original. While the original can be described as a war simulation, this is more of a war game. And for a game that keeps making me forgo sleep and keep saying "Just 1 more battle, Just 1 more battle" is surely doing something right.
Overall Rating: 9.0 / 10
If you are a fan of the original, this may disappoint you a little as it is not as indepth i feel, but it is still a worthy purchase as it definitely has the right XCOM spirit and definitely respects the franchise. If you are a fan of strategy games in general, this game will be worth your time.
If you have never touched a strategy game, do give it a try as it is rather easy to pick up, yet really fun to play. Excellent effort done, and i look forward to the sequel.

While the game is an incredibly enjoyable platformer/shooter roguetype, make no mistake; you will die and die again. Risk of Rain rewards players for perserverance and adaptiveness on the fly. The random enemy generation and plethora of upgrades to build a unique character each run combined with the stellar co-op multiplayer keep the game feeling fresh even after double-digit hours played. The difficulty meter that gradually raises over the course of your run is an interesting design feature, keeping you on your toes and always moving. One issue however is the sometimes monotonous way you are forced to dispatch enemies by simply kiting them. Another somewhat questionable characteristic is the balancing, or lack thereof. It is very clear that some classes are much more powerful than others.
Those who can muster the will and ability to master its cruel alien terrains will find a ton of fun in this indie title. 8.0/10

is the unofficial
game we always wanted! The horrific plight of starship engineer Issac Clark aboard the U.S.G Ishimura perfectly replicates the feeling of isolation and suspense of Ridley Scott's classic, while also innovating and branching out on its own right to create an impeccable homage to sci-fi horror which continually surprises and rewards with each astoundingly well thought out design decision.
Immersion is everything to
. The complete lack of a standard HUD or in level load screens, inventory and menus screens that don't pause the game and the fact you are never taken away from Issac's perspective whether during gameplay or in menus, all combines to ensure you are never taken out of the experience. I have to commend the developer for what they have done with the HUD, placing standards like health and ammo counts not on a floating display but physically on the character and weapon at hand. It is one of the most original ideas I've seen in any game for years that takes something simple and makes it elegant, and taken as a whole this is one of the most atmospheric games ever released.
Gameplay is equally ingenious in that it takes something we know, in this case the shooting mechanics of a game like
, and turns it on its head. Disregarding the tried-and-true "aim for the head" mantra, you are required to dismember the tentacle like arms and legs of your enemies piece by piece, chopping them up into limbless husks in a concise and diligent manner conserving as much ammo as you can in the process. It's as gruesome as it sounds, but more than just an all out gore fest it lends a more strategic and thoughtful approach to combat that asks you to hold still and be precise with your shots in the midst of extreme peril, which gives it a feel all its own and playing other games afterwards starkly outlines how traditional many of them are in comparison.
Of course none of this impromptu surgery would be possible without one of the best weapons in video game history: the plasma cutter. A tool of Issac's trade, it shoots a beam razor sharp plasma perfect for severing the many appendages of your foes, and can be rotated for an even more exact cut. It's so good in fact that it actually forms one of my few complaints, as the other more rudimentary tools of destruction are far less interesting and practical to use, to the point I actively tried to avoid having to take them out. Thankfully after a few upgrades that became a very rare occasion, and the plasma cutter certainly is enough to make up for the lack of other useful weapons.
Despite going on more than a half decade at the time of this review, this is still an exceptionally good looking game which stands testament to how impressive it was to begin with. The environments are vivid and cohesive without growing sterile, and the expert use of shadows is still unmatched by many more recent games. Reference quality sound design sells the experience, almost demanding a high quality sound system or pair of headphones to fully appreciate. The plot never intrigued me in any great amount, but like
before it much of the exposition is left in the form of audio diaries and notes which provided a great deal of backstory on the events before your arrival, and help compensate for the otherwise lackluster narrative that only barely covers the typical video game chicanery of sending you to every corner of the ship in a rather contrived manner.
One final note isn't so much a con as simply something that should be stated. Despite its horror trappings
is still an action game first and foremost. After the first hour or so enemy patterns and scare tactics become easy to spot and predict, which while not detracting from the experience may disappoint some hoping to be frightened out of their wits. That said it is still very apt at getting your pulse up through the ever constant gloom and tenseness of its atmosphere, which even if it doesn't scare you should be more than enough to excite and increase your heart rate.
For anyone not turned off by the extremely graphic violence,
is a must play. It excels at pulling you into its world and keeping you absorbed in it through an increadible atmophere that goes almost unmatched. With every step forward developer
(now renamed to the more fitting Visceral Games) show an acute knowledge of game design, never content to reiterate something already done without making it their own, and is does more for the horror action genre than probably any game since RE4. I was blown away with every passing moment, and cannot wait to dive into what horrors the future games hold. If you haven't already taken a trip aboard the Ishimura, there's no better time than now to do so, as I can assure you its a journey you won't soon forget.

Yeah, this is everything KF1 does and done better.
Runs excellent -not flawlessly, but more stable than the original- on middling hardware. I can't say I've had literally no problems, but I can say I can't recall the last time a match crashed out. As compared to KF1 where I can recall always praying the host doesn't ragequit and screw me out of my kill xp.
Maps are good alone and make for great team play -though a server full of blithering ♥♥♥♥wits are still the death of a Demo or Sharpshooter trying to kill big targets- and they have solid terrain variety within them. Lots of chokepoints, wide open spaces, and tricky transition passages. Good difference in location atmosphere.
Zed time is less disruptive and feels more useful; match pacing in general is quicker. FAR less waiting for a zed to shamble over and get things going. Less empty map space, faster welding -KF2 is leaner, more focused. KF1 feels like a Counterstrike mod, KF2 feels like an actual professionally developed and polished commercial product.
Weapons are decently varied and balanced. Getting your Perks starting weapon is an idea entirely worth it's time. This does mean finding a stray weapon is less of a windfall, but that's probably for the best (free armor is still great).
Cross-Perk gearing is more viable as weapon weights are solidly standardized. Big♥♥♥♥♥10kg weapons are no long the obvious all-important choice nor stupidly restrictively heavy (hello M99).
Generic weapons contribute to the Perk equipped -no "off leveling" Sharpshooter while slogging through your first wave. Parrying is your friend, btw, so that lightweight and cheap Katana is a damn good use of 2kg against getting rushed by Patty.
The Sharpshooter/Gunslinger division is sensible and effecient; Gunslinger plays very nicely different by getting to combine mobility with damage output both precise and steady. Sharpshooter can borrow some of that or like 50%+ bonus damage for holding still instead.
Commandos are better both solo and as a foundational  teamplay class.
Demos are far better as they now contribute more, have a cheap viable starting weapon, and can ♥♥♥♥ing booby trap doors.
(that's what an orange welding seam means fyi. stop ♥♥♥♥ing unwelding them)
Not a gigantic fan of the Berserker, but I never was. New Nailgun's a nice addition though, and that you can get Zerker xp by fighting near someone else's Zerker is a nice touch.
Overall Perks are good with maybe the starting Sharpshooter struggling. Personal faves are Firebug, Medic, Commando, and Gunslinger. Maybe also Demo.
Perk leveling and branching are both fine. No more getting stuck on "kill 100 Stalkers" while you're already 100k past the AR damage benchmark. The Perk branches do a lot to make each class feel more like itself -the Zerker and Commando can both be strong foundations for using other classes weapons or a hell of a lot more punishment as specialists while the Firebug is less versatile- though some of the balance selections are odd -see Flaratov v. Free Ammo. Rather have one of them make dead zeds into illumiunating bonfires instead.
Plays just fine with a dualshock or XBox controller -no, not using aim assist either.
Complaints? Getting stuck on random crates while back-peddling. Not enough vertical mobility -usually can't jump on cars. Night vision is ..odd. I have yet to be sure when it's on or how to make it activate. Music's not as good either, dunno why. Hosting is stupidly complex now, bleh.
FYI devs? The whole "you died and the local GLADOS Npc snarks you" thing is over. Make it ♥♥♥♥ing go away.
Also while character selection is in general is solid enough Rae makes me cringe. Interestingly none of the new survivors are particularly irritating -even Rae's mostly just bland- nor obnoxious cliche'd in that "omg Tracer no" way. Would like another female character who _isn't_ Rae.
The key-lootbox-dlc thing? Don't like the vibe coming off it. Random loot bought with RL $ is sketchy AF; KF1 was burdened by a glut of dubiously worthwhile DLC but this isn't much better.
Worth $30? Easily. Tons of violent, bloody, engaging fun; a serious improvement over the formidably solid prequel.
Note: I see reviews freaking the ♥♥♥♥ out about the development process.
I am utterly indifferent to whatever that moral panic is about; I care about the end product far more than I ever would care about if the devs are making the game "my way." And anybody ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thier pants about "broken promises" knows nothing about actually developing anything worthy of the term "project." More gets promised than is usually delivered; this is how complex, enormous, and expensive projects go. This is how everything you've ever liked in gaming went and the only difference is that now you can see it happening.

I cannot recommend this game to anyone that has enjoyed the first Killing Floor. Some will say "just don't compare it to the other game; it's its own thing". You'd be right. Killing Floor 2 just happens to be a game that shares the same name as the first, it has the same enemy names, the same perks, leveling system, and weapons, but it is not the Killing Floor we know and love. With that being said, I can only compare it to 1 because it was made by the same company, and no other game is quite like the idea of Killing Floor itself.
It's missing something that made the first game feel great to play, and I believe it has to do with the skill ceiling; in KF1 you can play effectively even with a level 0 perk, whereas in KF2 perk level means a lot more now that there are perk abilities. Aside from that, there is very little separating a new player from a seasoned one, which is something very noticable in KF1.
Larger enemies feel like unfun bullet sponges where everyone has to shoot them or half the team will wipe. KF1 teams can dedicate a single person per large enemy and make quick work of said enemy. The game itself just feels like it has been dumbed down so that it works well with the PS4 port, but as of writing the game has only been on PC where options/customizations feel really left out (e.g. the voice command menu is now a wheel with little option; KF1 had several voice menus, and even contextual voice commands that can be made into keybinds such as siren and husk callouts)
At the end of the day, KF2 is great for mindless mouse clicking with friends and strangers alike. I can only play at maximum for about 2 hours before I find myself getting bored and moving onto something else. Very different from playing an entire day of KF1.
I don't know who this game is catered towards. The new players love this game but tend to not stick around for very long, or the long-time KF1 veterans who will play this game until its last server shuts down but currently hate where the game is going in terms of development.

Откладывал прохождение этой игоры как только смог, знал, что веселье будет коротким, а новых модулей от сообщества ещё толком нет, от разработчиков только в октябре, но не смог больше тянуть - сел и взахлеб прошел последнюю битву. Чувство детской радости и настоящего разочарования вперемешку, хотя на этом можно и закончить короткую заметку, но все же.
Когда проект увидел на кикстартере, начал активно ждать - в арты сразу же влюбился, сеттинг был знаком по игре на сеге, врать не буду, ничего тогда не понимал, просто бегал и исследовал локации.
Появился предзаказ в стиме, сразу захотелось приобрести, но, учитывая прошлые разочарования, решил сначала таки ознакомиться с геймплейными видео и прочими штуками из интернетов. Вот тогда и случился приступ ярости - восьми-десяти часовая флешка, без какой-либо реиграбельности, абсолютно линейная с боями без челленджа.
После долгих и мучительных сомнений все же приобрел.
Начал исследовать ролевую систему - проста, изящна и гибка, освоить её можно просто поглядев на древо умений, ничего сложного нет. Сама игра дерзко устраивает покатушки по киберпанк-рельсам, свернуть никуда не удастся - как выяснилось, не только из-за лени разработчиков сделать что-то огромное и массивное, сам движок и его особенности не позволяют. Пока что. Бои в самом начале никакущие - можно лениво тыкать на все подряд, осваивая механику (так сильно похожую на последний xcom), в самом конце хочется размахивать руками и громко ругаться, внезапные перемены сложности выбивают из колеи.
К слову, в концовочке и последних эпизодах самый смак.
Но веселье, как я выше писал, было недолгим. Нуар закончен, дело об убийстве бывшего коллеги раскрыто, у каждого персонажа своя концовочка (ах, какие персонажи!) и вот собственно все, печальные титры идут безмерно долго, мельтеша записями никнеймов всех бейкеров.

Risk of Rain, simply put, is a sci-fi action-adventure rogue-like game.
Risk of Rain, specifically put, is the most amazing badass side-scrolling sci-fi shooter I have ever seen. It has more content than almost any other rogue-like game I've ever seen, and is close to perfection in every way.
Pros:
-Around 15 different classes to choose from, each with their own upsides and downsides to get used to.
-Dozens of different items to collect, each giving you specific passive boosts or qualities to add a little quality to what will almost always be your short life.
-A great many activated items, which can do anything from launching missiles to placing a torch that fears and damages enemies to even sacrificing a small portion of your health to instantly kill the closest enemy to you (yes, that includes BOSSES).
-Several different environments, all with their own unique layouts.
-A very uniquely challenging aspect: as time forges on, so does the difficulty. In other words, the longer you live, the less likely you are to continue living.
-Although not many, there are a few story elements, such as item and monster logs to show you what you're dealing with.
Cons:
-Even the easiest difficulty is very challenging for new players. It took me around 5 games to get used to it enough to get past the 2nd stage.
-You begin with only the Commando class, which most players consider the worst class in the game. It also can take quite a lot of effort and skill to unlock some of the characters.
-Monsters have a tendency to spawn very frequently once you reach around the 6-minute mark.
-You must activate a teleporter to transition between levels, and during this time, monsters spawn much more often than they already do, and a powerful boss spawns to make it an even greater challenge to live.
-Pressing Ctrl+Esc in the middle of the game will hide it as normal, but there isn't always something in the taskbar for you to click to pull it back up. Even in windowed mode, the taskbar shows no signs of the game being open. If this happens, it also becomes impossible to reopen it with Steam without restarting the computer, as it will bring up a window saying the "app is already running". (NOTE: Even if this happens, it may randomly add itself to the taskbar, allowing you to re-enter the game and resume play as normal. However I am not sure of what causes this to happen.)
-Exiting a current run brings it to an end instead of saving progress, just as if you had died.
In my belief, however, the ups heavily outweigh the downs. This game is obscenely fun and difficult to stop playing once you've started.
9/10
P.S. The Commando class is actually a good one to have to start out with. He is capable of hitting enemies on the edge of the screen with ease, and his attacks can knock back most enemies, keeping them at bay temporarily. He also has a dodge roll that grants him immunity to all damage until he completes the roll. Overall, he can be very easy to get used to, and getting a lot of items that apply on-hit effects can be ridiculous on him.

The biggest compliment that I can give Dead Space is that it gives me an experience akin to watching the Aliens movies, which I love.
You play as silent protagonist Isaac Clarke who boards the USG Ishimura in order to discover what has happened on board the ship. THe motivation which drives Isaac further forward is his desire to be reunited with his wife who happens to be on board the Ishimura.
Dead Space has a variety of monsters to face and a few distinct and unique ways in which to deal with them thanks to the weapons Isaac has at hand and which are available for him to purchase later in the game. While the weapon choices are fairly limited, the different ways in which they can be used to eliminate your enemies will allow you to have a variety of options in which to play the game.
The graphics still hold up and the setting is eerie enough, with the sound effects truly spectacular if you are using a proper sound system or headphones. While the story and characters may not be the strongest, those are not the reasons you play a game like Dead Space.
If you are looking for a third person survival shooter to scare the ever-loving crap out of you, I cannot recommend this game highly enough.

Yeah, this is everything KF1 does and done better.
Runs excellent -not flawlessly, but more stable than the original- on middling hardware. I can't say I've had literally no problems, but I can say I can't recall the last time a match crashed out. As compared to KF1 where I can recall always praying the host doesn't ragequit and screw me out of my kill xp.
Maps are good alone and make for great team play -though a server full of blithering ♥♥♥♥wits are still the death of a Demo or Sharpshooter trying to kill big targets- and they have solid terrain variety within them. Lots of chokepoints, wide open spaces, and tricky transition passages. Good difference in location atmosphere.
Zed time is less disruptive and feels more useful; match pacing in general is quicker. FAR less waiting for a zed to shamble over and get things going. Less empty map space, faster welding -KF2 is leaner, more focused. KF1 feels like a Counterstrike mod, KF2 feels like an actual professionally developed and polished commercial product.
Weapons are decently varied and balanced. Getting your Perks starting weapon is an idea entirely worth it's time. This does mean finding a stray weapon is less of a windfall, but that's probably for the best (free armor is still great).
Cross-Perk gearing is more viable as weapon weights are solidly standardized. Big♥♥♥♥♥10kg weapons are no long the obvious all-important choice nor stupidly restrictively heavy (hello M99).
Generic weapons contribute to the Perk equipped -no "off leveling" Sharpshooter while slogging through your first wave. Parrying is your friend, btw, so that lightweight and cheap Katana is a damn good use of 2kg against getting rushed by Patty.
The Sharpshooter/Gunslinger division is sensible and effecient; Gunslinger plays very nicely different by getting to combine mobility with damage output both precise and steady. Sharpshooter can borrow some of that or like 50%+ bonus damage for holding still instead.
Commandos are better both solo and as a foundational  teamplay class.
Demos are far better as they now contribute more, have a cheap viable starting weapon, and can ♥♥♥♥ing booby trap doors.
(that's what an orange welding seam means fyi. stop ♥♥♥♥ing unwelding them)
Not a gigantic fan of the Berserker, but I never was. New Nailgun's a nice addition though, and that you can get Zerker xp by fighting near someone else's Zerker is a nice touch.
Overall Perks are good with maybe the starting Sharpshooter struggling. Personal faves are Firebug, Medic, Commando, and Gunslinger. Maybe also Demo.
Perk leveling and branching are both fine. No more getting stuck on "kill 100 Stalkers" while you're already 100k past the AR damage benchmark. The Perk branches do a lot to make each class feel more like itself -the Zerker and Commando can both be strong foundations for using other classes weapons or a hell of a lot more punishment as specialists while the Firebug is less versatile- though some of the balance selections are odd -see Flaratov v. Free Ammo. Rather have one of them make dead zeds into illumiunating bonfires instead.
Plays just fine with a dualshock or XBox controller -no, not using aim assist either.
Complaints? Getting stuck on random crates while back-peddling. Not enough vertical mobility -usually can't jump on cars. Night vision is ..odd. I have yet to be sure when it's on or how to make it activate. Music's not as good either, dunno why. Hosting is stupidly complex now, bleh.
FYI devs? The whole "you died and the local GLADOS Npc snarks you" thing is over. Make it ♥♥♥♥ing go away.
Also while character selection is in general is solid enough Rae makes me cringe. Interestingly none of the new survivors are particularly irritating -even Rae's mostly just bland- nor obnoxious cliche'd in that "omg Tracer no" way. Would like another female character who _isn't_ Rae.
The key-lootbox-dlc thing? Don't like the vibe coming off it. Random loot bought with RL $ is sketchy AF; KF1 was burdened by a glut of dubiously worthwhile DLC but this isn't much better.
Worth $30? Easily. Tons of violent, bloody, engaging fun; a serious improvement over the formidably solid prequel.
Note: I see reviews freaking the ♥♥♥♥ out about the development process.
I am utterly indifferent to whatever that moral panic is about; I care about the end product far more than I ever would care about if the devs are making the game "my way." And anybody ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thier pants about "broken promises" knows nothing about actually developing anything worthy of the term "project." More gets promised than is usually delivered; this is how complex, enormous, and expensive projects go. This is how everything you've ever liked in gaming went and the only difference is that now you can see it happening.

I cannot recommend this game to anyone that has enjoyed the first Killing Floor. Some will say "just don't compare it to the other game; it's its own thing". You'd be right. Killing Floor 2 just happens to be a game that shares the same name as the first, it has the same enemy names, the same perks, leveling system, and weapons, but it is not the Killing Floor we know and love. With that being said, I can only compare it to 1 because it was made by the same company, and no other game is quite like the idea of Killing Floor itself.
It's missing something that made the first game feel great to play, and I believe it has to do with the skill ceiling; in KF1 you can play effectively even with a level 0 perk, whereas in KF2 perk level means a lot more now that there are perk abilities. Aside from that, there is very little separating a new player from a seasoned one, which is something very noticable in KF1.
Larger enemies feel like unfun bullet sponges where everyone has to shoot them or half the team will wipe. KF1 teams can dedicate a single person per large enemy and make quick work of said enemy. The game itself just feels like it has been dumbed down so that it works well with the PS4 port, but as of writing the game has only been on PC where options/customizations feel really left out (e.g. the voice command menu is now a wheel with little option; KF1 had several voice menus, and even contextual voice commands that can be made into keybinds such as siren and husk callouts)
At the end of the day, KF2 is great for mindless mouse clicking with friends and strangers alike. I can only play at maximum for about 2 hours before I find myself getting bored and moving onto something else. Very different from playing an entire day of KF1.
I don't know who this game is catered towards. The new players love this game but tend to not stick around for very long, or the long-time KF1 veterans who will play this game until its last server shuts down but currently hate where the game is going in terms of development.

You play as silent protagonist Isaac Clarke who boards the USG Ishimura in order to discover what has happened on board the ship. THe motivation which drives Isaac further forward is his desire to be reunited with his wife who happens to be on board the Ishimura.
Dead Space has a variety of monsters to face and a few distinct and unique ways in which to deal with them thanks to the weapons Isaac has at hand and which are available for him to purchase later in the game. While the weapon choices are fairly limited, the different ways in which they can be used to eliminate your enemies will allow you to have a variety of options in which to play the game.

The last entry of Rocksteady's famous Arkham series has drawn to a close. The Arkham trilogy was by far the best comic book related game that I have ever played. I remember how amazing the combat, atmosphere, pacing, tone, and story-telling that Arkham Asylum had delivered. Many like myself thought 'wow, finally a comicbook based game worth our time and it's Batman!' Batman is arguably the most iconic and popular comic book protagonist in history. I wouldn't call him a superhero, but a hero non-the-less. There are so many layers as to what makes Batman so great! He is the foundation of inspiration for many comic book heroes today.
How does Arkham Knight compare to the rest? The pinnacle being Arkham City to most Arkham fans.
The Batmobile: It's fun to drive and even more fun to destroy armor with, to use as a tool for many things. The incorporation was handled both well and poorly; it was handled well in terms of using the raw power of this vehicle to not only get around, but to do things that Batman could not do otherwise, such as pull up an elevator. However, as neat as the Batmobile is and as much as I adore the design that went into it… I felt that was an intrusion on some of the gameplay. Such as certain boss battles. I didn't feel like it was forced onto me throughout the game. After upgrading the eject function, I would usually do this because it was faster to travel by air gliding than by the Batmobile. It's handling was handled well. It is a hybrid tank/APC/Supercar. It weighs a lot! It's not going to handle all that well. I found the weighty feel while driving a welcoming balance.
Comba/gameplayt: Same base formula, bur more fine tuned for the better. Arkham Knight has the best combat out of the three titles. It's not just the new Batsuit either, which, is my favorite looking Batsuit of all time! Batman seems to fight with more ferocity, he is also faster; hitting harder. The combat makes you feel more like a bad♥♥♥♥♥than ever before all while still being challenging. The multi-fear takedown ability is a very awesome feature that isn't overplayed, yet perhaps a bit underplayed. Combat is also much more fluid than the other Arkham titles. Gliding and diving and everything else is also an improvement. The downside is that the personal connection with Batman's villains just isn't there, not like it was in the two previous titles. It feels disconnected.
Story: This game, like the others is story driven at its core. I enjoyed the story, but I didn't quite feel the essence of Batman from the comics like I had with AA and AC. The story had its moments and had its moments of frustration. I won't delve too much into the story, but I will say that Arkham City has a better story overall… not by much, but better.
Graphics: The visuals are completely stunning! I loved the art direction, the atmosphere was perfect for the night that the Batman would die. nVidia works made for an even more immersive experience, making the ambience much more dismal. Gotham City isn't as well lit or as colorful as it was in AC. Different art direction, though subtle in many ways. My system had no issues handling the game at 1080P. I even tried it out on my 4K TV where my average FPS was about 28-30 with nVidia features turned off and it looked breathtaking! Textures appeared to be all high-res. I really loved how they captured the details of the Batsuit!
Audio: I enjoyed the rumble of the Batmobile, the explosions, the gliding and diving, the sound of the rain pelting off of my cape. The VO work was top notch quality!
It's fun being Batman! I place Arkham Knight more or less on par with Arkham City. The only thing that irritated me was that there were boss battles where you rely too heavily on the Batmobile. The challenges are fun! There is an abundance of content and criminals to lockup.

I think the best strategy for improvement is the same as studying for a test. Study until you've maxed out for the day, wait at least 2 days, then come back. Sleep reinforces learning, and yes, the game is a learning process. As fast as it is, muscle memory and learning patterns are a key part of gameplay. Buyers beware: It often gives me serious disorientation to the point of motion sickness. Your mileage may vary.

Upon first starting this game, you'll realize that there are no "Easy" or "Medium" difficulty settings. Keeping this in mind, you nervously select the first mode you see: "Hexagon," or "Hard" difficulty. You'll immediately not be able to breathe or blink as your tiny triangle first appears on the screen, mostly likely dying within a few seconds, obliterated against a flashing, rotating wall. Try as you might, you just can't seem to get past the first few seconds of the game. Occasionally you might get lucky and add a few more seconds onto your personal best. All the while, the only thing on your mind is dodging the shapes; nothing else in the world is more engrossing and entrancing when this game sucks you in with its trippy yet simple graphics and absolutely killer 8-bit soundtrack. Eventually you get frustrated enough to quit the game; that annoying female voice reminds you of your defeat with a dismissive "GAME. OVER." every time you mess up, and it's been getting on your nerves. This is the point where some people never come back to this game. However, if you're like me, you come back the next day to try again. This game, while very daunting at first, becomes much more doable with practice. Through the countless times you hear that annoying disembodied voice proclaim your demise, the feeling of achieving a new high score is something truly incredible.

Can be a bit glitchy; make sure you delete your autosaves before quitting and there's some slowdown if you load a game from an already running game. Rare crashes and all aliens are always in groups that only become active when you see them, then dramatically scatter. A decently large but still limited number of maps, not randomly tile generated like the old games. But this is praise by exception; everything else about this game is masterful with plenty of throwbacks to the original series and its structure while still adding plenty of new content and concepts.

While no doubt a controversial PC release, most, if not all, of the technical issues this game launched with have been well ironed out at this point. And outside of that I'd dare to say that Arkham Knight, while maybe not as exciting as previous titles in the series, is a great game.
As far as gameplay goes, the freeflow combat system is still an incredibly fun and satisfying gameplay system to battle with, and the predator encounters are still tense and engaging. But both of these systems lack the shine they once had when the series first began all those years ago due to general franchise fatigue. But I can't imagine any way to make any real groundbreaking improvments on either front.
The introduction of a playable batmobile seems to have been an attempt to battle this fatigue, and in some respects it succeeds. I found it exhilarating to race through the streets, chasing down enemies and completing races. But while they are fun at the start, on the whole the tank battles sections are not varied or complex enough to be very engaging. There is also an extremely dissappointing absence of interesting boss fights, which the series has lauded for in past titles. Almost every boss encounter is a slight variation of either the freeflow, predator, or tank battles systems.
The legendary setting of Gotham City has also never been more detailed and full of life though. And not only in any other game, but also any other medium. It is an absolute blast to glide around Gotham and appreciate all the care and detail that was put into its construction. But the lack of complex interior environments is a dissapointment.
The game's story is maybe its most impressive feat, and is anchored by a miriad of outstanding performances. The pacing is outstanding with each story beat being followed by an even better one. It has such an incredibly strong start, which it confidently builds on until the very end. Never before has there been such an enthralling narrative that successfully delves into Batman's mental and emotional psyche.
But with that being said, my biggest complaint (in terms of both the story and entire game) is that many iconic Batman villians are given a bit of the short stick in their side missions. Characters that have dense wonderful stories in the comics; like Hush, Deacon Blackfire, and Ra's al Ghul; are quickly and unceremoniously rushed out the door in an obvious attempt to ties up all the series' loose ends. And while I consider this a true travesty, I'll still confidently say that Batman Arkham Knight is a great game.
