This is easily one of my favorite games. Now I haven't played it much, but I love it so far. There is a lot to do like prepare for an attack or build things in your cities to make them stronger or better. If you think this is a simple board game, you'd be wrong. There is a lot more too it than managing units and building like making peace treaties and getting city states to like you. Everything blends together so perfectly that once you learn the basics you'll be hooked in no time! Of course that's my experience and you might not like this game. It may seem confusing at first, because it is a big game so I would recommend you watch a tutorial before you even start the game up. I still don't even know what some things do or how they work completely. The nice thing is that this game is clearly multiplayer so you can dominate the world together. Depending on what difficulty you play... I honestly have only played the 2nd easiest difficulty. The first is way too easy and the 2nd is also really easy but a good place to start out in my opinion. Here is some advice: don't attack city states! It is useless! Also, it is okay if you are denounced when playing an easy difficulty because if you are playing right you should be OP compared to the other civs. One thing I was confused about was ocean when I started playing- It is possible to go over it, you just need more advanced technology, not just basic boat tech. You don't need flying units to go over oceans, so you can discover civs without it. If you are confused about this advice it is because you've never seen a tutorial. If that is the case, I recommend you watch one before even reading the reviews. Don't use the trailers on steam for that- they don't teach anything, they just show you gameplay.
So over all, this game is about:

-founding cities (nothing like grepolis if you know what that is)
-keeping cities happy
-nuking

-making peace with other civs. Or war.
-randomly finding you killed another civs spy
-laughing about how stupid easy dif. civs are
-watching hitler plays civ 5
-realizing city states are only helpful

1 year later UPDATE:
The latency issue I had last year is now gone. Finding servers with 2-15 ms is not a problem anymore.
Performancewise I stay at 60 fps locked with 2560x1440p with everything Ultra except for AA, blur and bloom turned off (don't like those techniques). Running on i5 3570k+GTX980.

Map variation is good, and it seems the community-maps have gotten better too.

Music could use a update, the songs are still OK but it's boring with the same ones. (Try playing with Red Alerts: "Hell March", it's so fitting!)
Who should buy this game then? Anyone who's got atleast 1 friend to play with, and who enjoys coop in terms of looking out for eachother. Extra plus if you like dry jokes, wet landscapes covered in gore and colorful microtransactions (which imo is A-OK!).

This game is phenominal.
Back when the FPS genre was something to look forward to, the Half-Life series was no exception.
In this installment of Half-Life, you are the almighty slayer/scientist Gordon Freeman, summoned again to defeat any opposition in your way, trying to take back Earth from the Combine.
The game itself has a rich story and wonderful lore. Half-Life 2 explaines everything to you without having to play the first one. In fact, in my opinion, Half-Life 2 handled storytelling much better than the first installment.
Every character has a personallity, from Alyx, Eli, Barney, Dr. Kliner, Etc. Even some of the "Single Serving NPS's" have a bit of personality. Like Father Grigori. Even NPS's that don't say much are well known, like the "Counsoling Couple". The dialogue is also a plus, my favorite line is from Barney, we all know what it is! "And if you see Dr. Breen, tell him I said, 'F*CK YOU'"! (Srry Barney "oweing beer" fans, if any out there lol)
The gun/game play is also top notch. The game itself has a world that you can interact with where other games don't let you. This promotes thought-provoking "puzzles" and makes the Gravity Gun one of the best weapons in Gaming Hsitory. Seriously, two whole levels promotes the Gravity Gun alone. The games design encourages felxable ways to dispatch your foes, and that makes the game much more interesting! Personally, I've played a run with only using the shotgun. (Except in RPG/GG Portions)
Graohics are good for the year 2004, and even today I still promote the graphics.
The game length will take you about 10-12 hours if you play on normal. However, this game will sucker you back in for sure. I did, that's why I got the "Orange Box" and steam edition. I NEEDED to play the game again.
Practically any PC can run this game, I've played this on a hoopty laptop from 2008 and it ran the game like a YouTube Video.
Overall, Half Life 2 is a great game that you should play at least one time. It's a fun and amazing experience.

A highly effective horror/survival/action/sci-fi adventure. Unfortunately pitted by some shockingly poor control porting and mouse acceleration. The game is frightening and shocking and powerful enough. It doesn't need fiddly inventory juggling to add suspense, and it doesn't need ammo or health packs at all. Sadly it does have these things. Terrible mouse problems (slightly remedied by turning off in-game vsync and turning ON control panel vsync (playing without vsync is for people who are lower class than rapists.)  Stupid, unweildy, frustrating and meaningless inventory and economy management that brings nothing to the table, and does not enrich the game whatsoever. The story is intriguing and mysterious, and the action (while slightly marred by the control/port issues) is tooth-grinding and ferocious. A great musical score, some wonderful and stunning set-pieces and generally excellent voice acting makes this one of my begrudgingly best gaming experiences I've had. The glaring flaws remind me of the flaws that were present in Mass Effect 1. As THAT series progressed, the developers got the picture, learned, and shed the fat to be left with the pure, perfect narrative masterpiece that is the Mass Effect trilogy. I don't expect exactly the same amount of rind to be cut off of the next two Dead Space games, but I hope the inventory, ammo, and controls are cleaner and more streamlined, leaving less between the game and my enjoyment of it.

This is a really interesting game with not a whole lot that has come out recently to compare it to. Basically its a turn based strategy game, and while not being as indepth as old school games like it, I think x-com does a good job of trying to bridge this type of game to people today. Overall, i'd recommend it for strategy fans who want something a little different, but for people who played the original x-coms or other turn based strategy like it, it will feel a bit watered down but even for you i'd say play it since it is a really fun game that sucks you in.

This is going to be a review strictly on the new Sharpshooter class. So far I've only gotten it to lvl 10.
I will be reviewing the weapons it uses, the perks, and it's play style. I'll compare it to other classes in KF2 and it's old KF1 counterpart.
First off, the weapons. The Lever Action Rifle or LAR is a powerful starting weapon, but not really one of the best. After the amunition update, most starting weapons the 9mm and other starter weapons got their ammo costs reduced, yet the LAR ammo cost is 30 dosh per 10 bullets, which is kind of pricy, and even when trying to conserve ammo, it is the one gun/class I can not save up enough dosh to purchase the top teir 1,500 weapon by round 4 on a 10 round match. It's reload bullet-by-bullet so it is very slow. I tend to find myself buying dual degals as a replacement.
The crossbow is good for killing sirens and husks early, but not much else because of it's one-shot-reload kind of weapon.
The M14 is a good mix between damage, ammo capcity, and fire rate, however the recoil may be a bit hard to handle at first. The ammo cost is decently proportionate to its weapon cost. It's magazine style reload makes it a much better weapon comapred to the LAR. Unfortunately its weight makes it incapable of carrying it and the rail gun at the same time.
The Rail gun is the head remover of scrakes and flesh pounds. Using the alt-fire and switching from the aim assist to manual aim 2x damage helps in quickly taking out the largest of targets. If you panic while being swarmed, the aim assist can help, although if you aren't a good, calm, aimer to begin with, maybe sharpshooter isn't the class for you.
The KNIFE IS DULL AS ALL HELL! It is the worst of all the class knives. It is a joke. It is more blunt and harder to remove a zeds head than the pulverizer (a sludge hammer!). You can not use it to remove a bloat's head, you'd have more success killing a bloat by unloading 2-4 magazines of 9mm into it's chest, no joke there.
The freezing grenade, its freezing radius seems a bit small, and the damage seems almost non-existant. It rarely kills crawlers, and even when thrown into the middle of a crawler swarm, it will maybe freeze like 3 or 4 at most.
Sharpshooter sufferes from the same thing medic does, not passively recieving any bonus damage with class weapons as you lvl up. You do however get bonus damage with headshots, which kinda helps if you are a perfect shot. The first 2 perks is kind of an easy pick, the 25% damage bonus for standing still helps tons since you don't have passive bonus damage for your level. The lvl 10 perk that gives 100% stun chance is much better, the crouching for the 30% damage makes you too imobile for this type of horde/zerg of zeds rushing game.
The Sharpshooter excels at taking down big zeds with the rail gun, or lots of trash zeds with the M14.
Or you can do both with the rail gun and dual degals, however you will probably be lvling your gunslinger class more than the sharpshooter class that way. But this was kind of the way Sharpshooter was designed to play in KF1, Rifles and backup dual pistols. It seems that the devs have not really let the sniper role stand on its own away from off-class weapons. With that said, it's kind of manditory that every class usually has a medic pistol though just for heals.
My rating of the Sharpshooter class out of 1-10 (10 being the best, 1 being the lowest)
I give it a 5.5.
It's a nice new/old class but can't stand alone with its own sharpshooter weapons, therefore lacking its identity as a class.
It's starting knife and weapon "upkeep" cost for ammo is horrible, leaving you mainly using your 9mm, which does not get bennifits from your perk traits.
It's up side is that it is probably the best class at dealing with Fleshpounds and Scrakes. However even with that, it can be difficult to land a clear head shot on them if you have a bad team who enrages them when no one is actually there to take them down.

If you loved Killing Floor 1 like i did then you will love killing floor 2. The gameplay is amazing and fun, the intensity and atmosphere of the game is engaging and captivating.
There is great detail put into the basics such as graphics as well as the updating of physics and mechanics to create solid gameplay in a setting where the environment reacts to your every action and move.
Sound effects and music tracks have had a great deal of effort put in that is both impressive and engaging.
The Perks are what you loved from the old killing floor 1 with major improvements and better gameplay mechanics.
The only issue would be slow developmental updates, but however seeing as tripwire takes great care in bringing each new update as perfect as possible (with minor fixes or updates to finalize it) it is not a major issue to be worried about.
Eventually after Killing floor 2 reaches half of the developmental time that killing floor 1 took it will be a very solid and nearly finished if not finished yet game, with many perks, great vanilla maps, lots of custom servers and custom maps powered and supported by the community.
I give this game a solid approval for purchase; you won't regret buying it especially when it costs less than half the price of the current or latest Triple A games.
I've already put many hours in it and i can say without a doubt it's got great potential for replayability and many future content updates from both tripwire and the community.

I only began playing the Batman Arkham games in the last 6 months. They have been some of the best single player games  I have ever played; definitely the best games I have ever played that I only spent $5 for.
I held off getting the Arkham Knight because I don't ever pay full price and then there was the horrid reviews and the fact that it was withdrawn being sold... twice.
Finally it went on sale right before and during the Lunar Sale so I took a chance because I was really wanting to see how it all ended and I loved the others. I have to say I was not disappointed with my purchase. I'm running it on an Alienware 17 R2 laptop with a gtx 970 via graphics amplifier and it runs perfect in 1080p and all settings turned to high. With all the nviida interactive options on I do get some FPS drops in certain areas so I turned off a couple and it runs smooth. This game is a beast and takes a lot of vram to run. I saw earlier reviews where people claim it's not "optimized" for pc but it's one of if not the best looking games I have played and you need an appropriate system to run it or turn some settings down. Make sure you have the latest drivers for your video card.  For me it runs beautifully.
The actual gameplay itself takes it to the next level. If you're a fan of the other arkham games this one won't disappoint. I see from other reviews that some love the batmobile, others hate it. For most of the game you have the option of using it to get around or you can grapple/glide to travel just like in arkahm city/origins. There are some parts where you have to use the batmobile but I enjoyed it. My only complaint was there are no proper boss fights like there were in the other installments; the confrontations mostly take place in the batmobile or as Preadtor encounters and didn't have the same gravity as boss fights in the other games and there was no proper last boss fight.
I know a lot of people are asking the question "does it work now?" For me and lots of recent reviewers with specs that meet the recommended requirements the answer appears to be, yes! If you're like me and never plan on owning a console ever again I say go for it! If you plan on holding a grudge against a company that dropped the ball on release (they did or they wouldn't have taken it down) well quit reading these reviews and find something else to do besides posting in the forums that the game is crap and still doesn't work when you haven't even played it.

South Park: The Stick of Truth is an rpg that has more of a Final Fantasy style of combat to it. But its not that at all what makes this game fun to play. Its ultimately the humor and the story that kept me playing.
The game starts out where all the kids are playing an rpg (This is also a follow up of the Black Friday episode), Cartman's humans vs Kyle's Droll elves, and they are all pretending to war against eachother for a stick they call the Stick of Truth. Its rather entertaining how much detail they go into on their made up world of Zaron, from Jimmy's house being made into a bar, to Kyle and Cartman's houses being the center point of their kingdoms.
But of coarse, South Park being South Park, the game's story gets even more crazy and random, from nazi zombies to a government agency pretending to be Taco Bell.
At the begining of the game you create your character, and there is quite a wide variety of hair styles and hair colors, though skin tone choices are sadly low, and you can't choose your gender either, sorry gals but you have to play as a boy. After making your character, you start in you're home in South Park, I won't say anymore to avoid spoliers, but just to let you know as part of the humor in the game, you're character does not say anything. You eventually get the choice of you're class, Fighter, Mage, Theif or Jew (Only South Park). All of them are unique in their moves and default armor. Unfortunatly, perks don't change by what class you choose, they are always the same which kinda hurts this game in replay value.
At some point later in the game you choose wether to join Cartman or Kyle's side, though I feel this should have been placed in the begining of the game, regardless, your choice only effects who you fight in the story line, either way both human and elf vendors will be available. At least you either get Stans sword or Butters hammer depending on the side you choose.
Sadly you are only aloud 1 buddy in combat, and there are only 6 buddies in total, but for the most part they are all useful, however, you will use Butters more often just for his professor chaos ability. It pops up at level 6 which doesn't really take long to get too. The game for the most part is really easy and Butters just makes it even easier past level 6, though later in the game there is a big difficulty spike. However I found out the reason why, is beacause enemies have their armor massively increased. This is really no problem since all you have to do is spam your armor shreading abilities.
Despite how much I love playing this game, my biggest pet peeve with this game is that it plays way to similar to Final Fantasy, by that I mean you level by just playing through the game (Levels have little influence since enemies get harder eveytime you level), levels just simply unlock better weapons and moves.
You can also get plastic surgery to turn your face into David Hasselhoff.
Now this won't effect the game's score but its still worth mentioning to potential buyers.

This game is borderline adult rating, since this is South Park there is a lot of humor in here that some may find disturbing (And thats putting it in a nice way).
There are jokes about, abortion, homosexuality, sex and crude humor (You can attack using farts).

To simply put it. Not the kind of game to be playing in front of anyone unless maybe they are a South Park fan too.

XCOM: Enemy Unknown is a game that caught many by surprise much like the aliens that invade Earth in this remake of a little game called UFO: Enemy Unknown, or XCOM: UFO Defense, depending on where you've played it. But instead of being a total disaster and the end of all of humanity as we know it, this game instead makes you feel empowered and makes more meaningful choices than games that would use the word "choice" as one of their bullet points. Not only that, it manages to stand out in a world dominated by First-Person Shooters.
XCOM is a Turn-Based Strategy game. While to anybody with a short attention span might find that idea utterly slow and boring, the game is anything but. The game gives you unprecedented control of how to defend the Earth from the alien menace ranging from prioritizing appealing to the Council that funds your project, to devoting your resources to supporting your soldiers on the ground. There's an addicting cycle to the game when you get new resources from a mission to put into researching some new gadget or weapon, then testing it out on the field and getting more resources to make even better equipment, and even better, the game's difficulty curves beautifully to your progress. There's also a great sense of satisfaction when you make a tactical or strategic error, then learn from it to improve your tactics in the long run and be a much better commander. You'll feel a lot smarter and a lot more bad♥♥♥♥♥when you turn your defeats into victories.
There's also something novel this day and age about a game you can "lose," and not just get a "game over" screen and load back a checkpoint to keep playing to some predetermined end point.
Now hopefully by this point, you're convinced, but if you're still unsure, check out the demo and see what the game is like for yourself.

Oh btw, i5 3570k, 8gb ram, 7870 hd, low settings, crashes from time to time but a blast to play. Anyone who doesn't recommend the game AND doesn't post his specs for everyone to see is an a-hole. Not to the game but to the ones still in the dark about buying it. Get your sugar honey ice tea straight, people. And with a GTX 970, everything was on high with 60+ fps. Mind your resolution.
The Arkham series has always been thought out as a story which every chapter trumps the previous one in some way. Asylum had the Scarecrow sections to view Batman's inside world. City had better boss fights, especially Mister Freeze, signifying both his and Batman's character as men of science, risks and decuction. Knight delves into Batman's psyche, dealing with Asylum's and City's reprecussions and introducing space invaders in tanks !
The division of the gameplay into brawling, stealth, headscratching, story, Batmobiling etc is done extremely well. There are tons of stuff to do and easter eggs to find. To prove that, I stayed on the first island and didn't even do the first mission until I had a video card good enough to handle this. That was about 20 hours of kicking♥♥♥♥♥and stopping joyrides on foot. I found two side missions, figured out the subtleties of Freeflow (for the 3rd time), spotted riddle locations, a Royal Flush Gang poker club and run people over and to my delight, I saw 3 locations in the horizon.
I started out the game and 10 hours in, I wondered if I could see the Asylum and City from where I was. And to my surprise, I spotted them ! Only then to trump myself and spot Wayne Manor in the mountains ! There are even newspapers on the ground with geeky headlines.
But enough about detail, RS is a monster at those. Freeflow has gotten a huge upgrade here thanks to the web-like upgrade system which is now tied to story and side missions. You cannot earn XP differently so it makes sense to try something different once in a while, not just for a break but also as a sense of pragmatism. Batman NEEDS an upgrade not because this a new game but because this an all out war. That's something most people don't get. You are dealing with trained soldiers here, medics start popping up in their ranks, able to support the other troops even on an offensive level and remember the ninjas from City ? Yeah, these are back too. They can use their friends as stepping stones for hightime. And all of these were trained by the Arkham Knight. Everything is Anti-Batman geared in this game (with one exception). You have friends too though, for some of the fights but to my surprise, they are optional. You can fight as one of Batman's allies or if you want, you can keep brooding. There are some clever workarounds the game throws at you for that when you are solving the riddles that made me chuckle.
The most subtle addition to the brawling though are the throw counters. The new suit comes with a hint that pressing the direction of the punch heading your way WITH the counter button at the same time, you don't just counter a move, you turn in into a grapple. And when you tripple counter this way, it is a great way to clear the immediate vicinity. Imagine pulling of DMC's Dante's stinger movie on the d-pad in multiple directions.
The sense of the scale makes the use of the Batmobile appropriate and it is awesome once you get your hands on it. You can eject from it, remote control it, use for out of the box thinking in riddles or conflicts in the street, drive on walls while upside down, takedown joyrides Burnout style etc. The best for me though were the tank battles. Like I said, it's like space invaders, evade the line of fire and then shoot. Rinse and repeat. For such an Anti-Batman though, the Knight sure didn't think about using manned tanks to bypass Batman no-kill ideology (this being the above exception I mentioned). But Batman being Batman would a workaround for that too. And since we are speaking of a city invasion, having drones makes sense since they do not sleep, require food or payment. Again, pragmatism. There were instances of 50 (!) drones being deployed at a time against you. And on hard difficulty, I imagine not being hit is the only way to survive.
As I started playing more, I was also given a legitimate reason why there is a multiple fear takedown in the game, it tied well to Bruce's thoughts about driveways from The Dark Knight, even though it can be a bit exploited since you only need a single silent takedown to recharge them. Hacking also made its way into the predator sections in a way that doesn't catapult you out of the action, giving you options like hacking drones. The rest of the options are funny as hell with the right upgrades for the gadgets. A gadget especially can be used for trolling. Heh.
So in general, the gameplay is the best of the series. Driving and shooting is great, flying is great, breaking legs is great, solving riddles is great. The game's first ending is a nice setup for the second which I have not yet seen. And I gotta say, I was spoiled for a thing or two and the game somehow managed to prove me wrong about things were gonna turn out. I yelled 'the f***' about 3 times and there are A LOT of twists in the game. No, The Knight's identity is not one of them but the conflict between him and Batman is well presented. There is also an acquaintance who keeps popping up and keeps you company but that would spoil things. He/she does a great job though. You are alone but not alone at the same time. Everything my review doesn't mention also works well.
So what doesn't work ? RS should do a bit more research into making a non-buggy open world game cause technical issues aside, there were times where thugs were getting stuck behing their own car and didn't jump over the hood to get me. My ride also fell through the street last night. Some people had a problem with the plethora of tanks in the final part of the game but I had no problem with them in that regard since I love the combat. What I do hate about the tanks is that they supplant a great character which could have been a great boss. Said character has nothing to do with tanks. Yet RS decided to stick him into one. I was thrilled to see he was in the game and that I would get to fight him but once the fight was over, my mind was screaming LAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAME. Also, in a manner of speaking, there are no Scarecrow Nightmare levels. That's two lost opportunities on villains. These two guys stand out because they are not being used as they should. The first one on -I have no idea what- grounds and the other on exclusivity grounds. That's stupid, plain and simple. And while we are on that, 240% completion nets you a gold bat emblem on your suit, that's it ?! I get that it's about the trip not the destination and I am gonna get there either way but come on.
The Arkhamverse has managed to do things even the comics don't have to balls to pull off. And that's why it will go in history, for me, as the best Batman oriented alternate universe. It's BTAS, The Dark Knight, DC comics and everything you love about Bruce in a package that is held back by this entry's serious technical issues and WB's complete lack of interest in fixing what they broke in the first place. One of my favourite games for quite a while. I'm not even sure where to start.
Its a very challenging and engaging game. You'll die again and again, and learn from it.
Every playable character (about 10 of them, and will be unlocked as you progress through the game and do achievements) have 4 "basic" abilites, which I always kind of related to moba games, altho mostly in how the abilities are presented.
The first one is a basic, low cooldown attack which you can spam.
The rest of them can vary between different kinds of dashes, blinks, aoe abilities and I could keep going. The point is that every kit fits the character extremely well, and despite it might seem simple at first glance, you'll eventually have (and will) master the kit if you want to survive long enough to win the game.
There is three difficulties to choose between, and when you get into the game, there is another difficulty bar - which will progressively be harder as time goes by and will eventually lead to bosses and elite creeps  spawning.
This means you'll have to maximize the amount of gold you receive per level, so you can get as many items as you can on one level, while finishing the level as fast as possible so you wont waste time, and end up at a hard difficulty with few items (which are essential to survival).
Speaking of items, there is a huge arsenal of different passive items, which have varying degrees of usefullness depending on what character you play as. Getting basic attack speed buffs, wont do you much good on a bolt sniper, but it might be good on others that are more dps focused. In that way, your build can vary in many ways (There are artifacts you can find, which among others, will make you able to specifically pick items, rather than getting random drops everytime - which is the norm).
Other than passive items, there are also a bunch of different actives, with a world of different uses - and works a lot like of your 4 basic abilities, but with a much longer cooldown.
It is very much worth mentioning it has both local and online coop available - although I havent found that to be very balanced, mostly due to its hard splitting items up, as you wont get much more gold despite being two or more people. Its still very fun however.
I personally love the "simplifed" pixel artstyle the game has, and has a lot of charm to it.
Lastly, but almost most importantly, the soundtrack by Chris Christodoulou, is insanely good. I've played for 50+ hours I think, and listened to the soundtrack outside of the game as well, and I'm still not bored of it.
(Chanson d'Automne will always have a special place in my heart
Also, you can beat giant magma worms up as a guy with huge fists. So satisfying.
Updated with artifacts that change the gameplay, adds even more content to the game. Possible to local/online coop as well.

The Arkham series has always been thought out as a story which every chapter trumps the previous one in some way. Asylum had the Scarecrow sections to view Batman's inside world. City had better boss fights, especially Mister Freeze, signifying both his and Batman's character as men of science, risks and decuction. Knight delves into Batman's psyche, dealing with Asylum's and City's reprecussions and introducing space invaders in tanks !
The division of the gameplay into brawling, stealth, headscratching, story, Batmobiling etc is done extremely well. There are tons of stuff to do and easter eggs to find. To prove that, I stayed on the first island and didn't even do the first mission until I had a video card good enough to handle this. That was about 20 hours of kicking♥♥♥♥♥and stopping joyrides on foot. I found two side missions, figured out the subtleties of Freeflow (for the 3rd time), spotted riddle locations, a Royal Flush Gang poker club and run people over and to my delight, I saw 3 locations in the horizon.
I started out the game and 10 hours in, I wondered if I could see the Asylum and City from where I was. And to my surprise, I spotted them ! Only then to trump myself and spot Wayne Manor in the mountains ! There are even newspapers on the ground with geeky headlines.
But enough about detail, RS is a monster at those. Freeflow has gotten a huge upgrade here thanks to the web-like upgrade system which is now tied to story and side missions. You cannot earn XP differently so it makes sense to try something different once in a while, not just for a break but also as a sense of pragmatism. Batman NEEDS an upgrade not because this a new game but because this an all out war. That's something most people don't get. You are dealing with trained soldiers here, medics start popping up in their ranks, able to support the other troops even on an offensive level and remember the ninjas from City ? Yeah, these are back too. They can use their friends as stepping stones for hightime. And all of these were trained by the Arkham Knight. Everything is Anti-Batman geared in this game (with one exception). You have friends too though, for some of the fights but to my surprise, they are optional. You can fight as one of Batman's allies or if you want, you can keep brooding. There are some clever workarounds the game throws at you for that when you are solving the riddles that made me chuckle.
The most subtle addition to the brawling though are the throw counters. The new suit comes with a hint that pressing the direction of the punch heading your way WITH the counter button at the same time, you don't just counter a move, you turn in into a grapple. And when you tripple counter this way, it is a great way to clear the immediate vicinity. Imagine pulling of DMC's Dante's stinger movie on the d-pad in multiple directions.
The sense of the scale makes the use of the Batmobile appropriate and it is awesome once you get your hands on it. You can eject from it, remote control it, use for out of the box thinking in riddles or conflicts in the street, drive on walls while upside down, takedown joyrides Burnout style etc. The best for me though were the tank battles. Like I said, it's like space invaders, evade the line of fire and then shoot. Rinse and repeat. For such an Anti-Batman though, the Knight sure didn't think about using manned tanks to bypass Batman no-kill ideology (this being the above exception I mentioned). But Batman being Batman would a workaround for that too. And since we are speaking of a city invasion, having drones makes sense since they do not sleep, require food or payment. Again, pragmatism. There were instances of 50 (!) drones being deployed at a time against you. And on hard difficulty, I imagine not being hit is the only way to survive.
As I started playing more, I was also given a legitimate reason why there is a multiple fear takedown in the game, it tied well to Bruce's thoughts about driveways from The Dark Knight, even though it can be a bit exploited since you only need a single silent takedown to recharge them. Hacking also made its way into the predator sections in a way that doesn't catapult you out of the action, giving you options like hacking drones. The rest of the options are funny as hell with the right upgrades for the gadgets. A gadget especially can be used for trolling. Heh.
So in general, the gameplay is the best of the series. Driving and shooting is great, flying is great, breaking legs is great, solving riddles is great. The game's first ending is a nice setup for the second which I have not yet seen. And I gotta say, I was spoiled for a thing or two and the game somehow managed to prove me wrong about things were gonna turn out. I yelled 'the f***' about 3 times and there are A LOT of twists in the game. No, The Knight's identity is not one of them but the conflict between him and Batman is well presented. There is also an acquaintance who keeps popping up and keeps you company but that would spoil things. He/she does a great job though. You are alone but not alone at the same time. Everything my review doesn't mention also works well.
So what doesn't work ? RS should do a bit more research into making a non-buggy open world game cause technical issues aside, there were times where thugs were getting stuck behing their own car and didn't jump over the hood to get me. My ride also fell through the street last night. Some people had a problem with the plethora of tanks in the final part of the game but I had no problem with them in that regard since I love the combat. What I do hate about the tanks is that they supplant a great character which could have been a great boss. Said character has nothing to do with tanks. Yet RS decided to stick him into one. I was thrilled to see he was in the game and that I would get to fight him but once the fight was over, my mind was screaming LAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAME. Also, in a manner of speaking, there are no Scarecrow Nightmare levels. That's two lost opportunities on villains. These two guys stand out because they are not being used as they should. The first one on -I have no idea what- grounds and the other on exclusivity grounds. That's stupid, plain and simple. And while we are on that, 240% completion nets you a gold bat emblem on your suit, that's it ?! I get that it's about the trip not the destination and I am gonna get there either way but come on.
The Arkhamverse has managed to do things even the comics don't have to balls to pull off. And that's why it will go in history, for me, as the best Batman oriented alternate universe. It's BTAS, The Dark Knight, DC comics and everything you love about Bruce in a package that is held back by this entry's serious technical issues and WB's complete lack of interest in fixing what they broke in the first place. I hope the years to come help fix this cause not only does the game itself deserve a spot on 2015's best games along with Wild Hunt, MGS V and Bloodborne but because it serves as an example of not bringing a ten yard pole to dinner with licensed games. This has been a great trilogy and for me, since I was here from the beginning, I hope this truly is the end. Bravo and good knight.

I had an eye on this game for a long time, as it was on my steamshop list and it looked pretty interesting. I bought it when it was sold as part of the humble bundle, what allowed me to share the game with some friends and therefore my experience is mostly multiplayer.
I am a big fan of retro/indie games in 2d graphics and as sidescrollers.
as it is does an awesome job in terms of strategic fight and hack 'n' slay.
The early stages are usually pretty easy for any character, your enemies are weak and basically explode on contact (not literally though). The longer you are playing, the harder the game becomes as the normal enemies get more life and elite enemies start spawning. If you are not blessed with fortune and you are not playing with artifacts (more details on them later) then the game becomes really difficult if you keep on rushing towards them as you did in the earlier stages, so that forces you to think more strategic, to learn the movesets of your enemies and how to kill them without having them hurting you.
Obviously the game gets easier the more experience you have in playing it. This gets us to another really interesting gamechanger, the
.
The artifacts are a way to change the game, to make it harder or "easier". As an example, one of the artifacts makes enemies drop explosives when they die, those hurt you and other enemies. That makes the game a lot more challenging as you cannot kill your opponents without keeping an eye onto your surroundings.
There are not too many moves and functions offered by the game, so there are not many buttons you have to press. You have 4 buttons for your skills, one for active items, one for jumping and the 4 arrow keys for moving around. There is no need to grab over half of your keyboard to hit a button to cast a spell. Perfect!
What I love even more than the keyboard ist the full gamepad support. Playing the game with an xbox controller ist far more comfortable than sitting right in front of the screen and additionally the controls are well portet to the controller so that you do not have any downsides if you do not use your keyboard.
The game is not done yet, there are a few glitches and bugs, but that does not make it a bad game at all. Everyone who enjoys roguelikes and 2D should take a look at this game as it offers many hours of entertainment and fun :)

TL;DR- Super Hexagon is amazing and well worth the $3. Heck I would even buy it for $10. Just be prepared to cry a little, and don't buy it if you get nauseous looking at flashy things or are prone to seizures.
This game..
Where should I start? At this point I've only had about 5 hours of playing it, but they have been some of the most frenzied and enjoyable hours of my life. I've got to say I've never seen a game like this, and I probably won't again for a long time.
In Super Hexagon, you control a triangle which orbits around a hexagon, centered on the screen. Around you, there are light and dark sections, made up of the space between vectors. Within those sections are walls of an outstanding color that come racing toward the Hexagon. You're essentially within a maze of color. If you get hit by a wall, it's game over and your score is submitted automatically so that friends can compete. It may seem like you're trapped, but there is always a way out, no matter how small the gap or how crazy the maneuver you're required to pull. Meanwhile, you have a bunch of crazy lights and effects bouncing around distracting you from the real goal, yet still managing to make the game so much better. On top of this, the music is classic, and superb.
Super Hexagon will provide you with 6 different levels, ranging from Hexagon -> Hyper Hexagonest, and from Hard -> Hardes♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You initially start with the first three- Hard, Harder, Hardest- but once you last for 60 seconds or longer on any of them, the levels go into hyper mode, and you also unlock their hyper mode forms in level select, where you can begin from the 60 second mark at 0 seconds.
The way the levels work is that each level has a set of 5-10 'gauntlets' or patterns that it cycles through randomly. So for example, Hexagon will start as a few stray blocks, then it might run its 3x 180 Degree pattern, then its Double Zig-Zag pattern, and then the hexagon in the center will... You'll see ;) . Each level has different patterns, though some are shared throughout the game. Hyper modes contain advanced versions of the patterns used in previous 'normal' levels.
Possibly one of the best things about this game is that it only requires two buttons to play. These are Left and Right Arrow, or Buttons 1 and 2 on your mouse. You can also connect a joypad if that's the way you roll. The fact that there is only one speed for the triangle (fast) makes things difficult. After a while you will adjust though, and learn to love the way the game works.
Another great feature of Super Hexagon is the fact that once you 'die' from hitting a wall, you can start over within one second, so even if you do somehow manage to rage within this beautiful setting, it probably won't last long, because you'll be off with another try. Other than this, there is an annoying voice when you lose that tells you it's 'gameover' and also one that says 'again' when you retry, but these can be disabled by accessing the game's files and moving the sound files.
On top of these things, this game can be booted up and you can be playing any level within 3 seconds. It loads SO FAST.
Now, do you think this game is worth it? Would you spend $3 (less than the price of a Big Mac) on this game? I think that you shoul go out and spend your three damn dollars on this amazing game!

Arkham Knight isn't a bad game, but it's a pretty lousy story. First, it's Batman in his Frank Miller mode. The Arkham series has always had a bit of the "Batman as authoritarian ubermench" quality. It's dialed up here to 11. The conceit of Batman having the Joker in his head is a pretty interesting idea, but much of the rest of the story is just awful. Gordon complaining that the police aren't prepared for the sort of violence they face, and thank God that there's someone who is just comes off as "Thank God there's a billionaire who's willing to do the dumbest thing conceivable to alleviate crime!" It's an OK game, and if you know the Arkham series, you know what you're getting from a game-play standpoint, but the story is just an authoritarian power fantasy. And the death of Barbara Gordon, the Catwoman as Damsel in Distress...well...Frank Miller would be proud.
UPDATE:
I've been trying to get back into this game since I just finished Life is Strange and it just feels like a chore to play this now. The mechanics are the same as every other Arkham game. Sure, you start with more or less all of the equipment. They don't make you go through the process of learning to be Batman yet again. That's nice. But the Batmobile is boring (compared to GTA or Saint's Row cars). The fights are all the exact same weary mechanics as all the other Arkham games with the exception that you can now use fear to make the one vaguely interesting scenario - the predator scenes - into something easier. I'm glad I got this game on sale. All the little holes and problems with the Arkham games just get magnified. The only redeeming quality is the Joker's commentary as you go about your business, but it's really not enough to save the game from "Yet Another Installment" syndrome.

Replaying Dead Space. What an experience. It's not scary, true, but the tension is palpable and the atmosphere is so well done. The sound design in this game is masterful.
The scarcity of resources makes every shot , every sliver of your health matter. You might run back the entire length of a level, just because your inventory now has room for an item that you saw on the ground somewhere.
Even within the game's simple mechanics, it offers a wide range of choices in how you want to evolve your character. Do you use many different weapons, or do you stick to a couple of them and upgrade them heavily? Or do you focus on more defensive attributes? Plenty of games do this, but Dead Space gives you no wiggle room, so choices matter more.
The way your character moves is really unique. Isaac Clarke is an engineer in a heavy suit rather than a soldier in body armour, and he uses tools and moves like a steamroller, with weight to each step and a claustrophobic field of view.
The story is alright, but what I like more is the world that's been created to set the game in. The whole space-religion angle, conflict with science, paranoia and fanaticism...
The game's interface, heads up display, inventory, even the aiming reticules for the weapons... everything is projected in the world, in front of your character. This was very refreshing when the game came out, maybe even innovative, and even today very few third-person games games use it properly.
The combat is satisfying as hell, with interesting mechanics like severing limbs and combining slow motion with a gravity gun. Enemies and weapons are varied and have different strategies.
And you get to curbstomp all manners of gory monsters, and punt mutated babies across rooms. What's not to love about that?

Ahh Dead Space! A game that I have finished numerous times on PC and even dared to get the Platinum trophy for the PlayStation 3. Now having finished the Impossible difficulty mode from my previous saved game (from years ago), I'm ready to play some more!
So to recap quickly, Dead Space is a fine exceptional game made by the evil EA, although, it is a franchise I hold dear in my book of great games. The game is heavily inspired from the likes of the DOOM franchise, for the scare and action factors and on SYSTEM SHOCK franchise for the great story and setting of the game. Other notable inspiration would be from sci-fi movies like the Alien, The Thing franchises.
PROS:
-Fantastic story! I really dig the whole thing even if it seems very "System Shock-ish".
-Incredible gruesome atmosphere. (Sci-fi + Horror + Gore = Awesomeness!)
-Adrenaline rush action... especially on the "Impossible Mode".
-Strategic dismemberment (you like headshots eh? forget those in Dead Space!)
-Cool upgrade system for your RIG and the Weapons.
-Quite scary (well, it was on my first playthrough then it gets very unsettling!).
-Cool mechanics.
-Gorgeous looking, even on today's timeframe.
-Impressive sounds and ambience
CONS:
-Limited frame rate which leads to #2 con...
-The infamous nasty and truly annoying INVISIBLE WALL bug after you pickup your first weapon, the Plasma Cutter. (A fix exist and you have to force the VSYNC and even the TRIPPLE BUFFERING through your GPU control panel).
-VSYNC was quite buggy on Dead Space release. It needed a patch for it to work properly.
-Atrocious mouse control at release and even post-patch, the mouse is still sluggish, especially on the camera.
-Repetitive mission objectives.
-Close quarter combat is troublesome.
RATING: 8.5 / 10

Arkham Knight isn't a bad game, but it's a pretty lousy story. First, it's Batman in his Frank Miller mode. The Arkham series has always had a bit of the "Batman as authoritarian ubermench" quality. It's dialed up here to 11. The conceit of Batman having the Joker in his head is a pretty interesting idea, but much of the rest of the story is just awful. Gordon complaining that the police aren't prepared for the sort of violence they face, and thank God that there's someone who is just comes off as "Thank God there's a billionaire who's willing to do the dumbest thing conceivable to alleviate crime!" It's an OK game, and if you know the Arkham series, you know what you're getting from a game-play standpoint, but the story is just an authoritarian power fantasy. And the death of Barbara Gordon, the Catwoman as Damsel in Distress...well...Frank Miller would be proud.
UPDATE:
I've been trying to get back into this game since I just finished Life is Strange and it just feels like a chore to play this now. The mechanics are the same as every other Arkham game. Sure, you start with more or less all of the equipment. They don't make you go through the process of learning to be Batman yet again. That's nice. But the Batmobile is boring (compared to GTA or Saint's Row cars). The fights are all the exact same weary mechanics as all the other Arkham games with the exception that you can now use fear to make the one vaguely interesting scenario - the predator scenes - into something easier. I'm glad I got this game on sale. All the little holes and problems with the Arkham games just get magnified. The only redeeming quality is the Joker's commentary as you go about your business, but it's really not enough to save the game from "Yet Another Installment" syndrome.

I -might- play this for the story, but with all the other problems, it's really not worth it.

Dead Space has an interesting story, but lacks polish in a lot of other areas. Like so many games, it introduces interesting concepts, only to execute them poorly. For instance, you sever the arms of aliens to kill them. The catch? Mouse control is awful. It requires precise aiming, and you can clearly tell that it's a console port by the way you are moving. In fact, I was forced to disable v-sync to even get the mouse working at all. A lot of other things work poorly, including AA (any type), loading saves (yes, loading saves), and simulated physics. It's also not immersive (probably due to the abundant issues) and therefore not intense/frightening at all.
I -might- play this for the story, but with all the other problems, it's really not worth it.

Risk of Rain brings something interesting to the "rogue-like" table by streamlining the learning process while manitaing a sense of indiviuality in it's characters. Characters have only four abilties available to them at anytime, as well as one slot for an active item that can be found in game. This makes each character a unique experience to play, without subjecting the player to a complex adjustment period. Of course this is a "rogue-like", and cheap deaths and frustration are to be expected in Risk of Rain. This game makes no attempt hold your hand, but if you wanted easy you'd probably be playing Candy Crush.
The graphics are simplistic but well rendered, invoking the style of early DOS games. The ambient music is nice and the game lore is interesting, albiet well hidden. The gameplay is appropriately difficult, but very addictive. A must have for the library of any "rogue-like" junkie, like myself.

As many of you may be eyeing this game because of this sale that is going currently, why I do believe it may still be worth the money that is being asked I still think the game and the developers need some big changes.
Pros:
- A great looking and performing game that is truly the graphical leader than the first game in the series.
- Great weapons with great animations.
- Great characters with great personality's, made you feel more in tune with the game.
Cons:
- The first thing that is most apparent is Tripwire, they don't listen to the community at all and go on personal agendas of making a tf2 like crate and key items system before creating all of the classes.
- The newly added resistance system, an example is the Firebug, he gets extra xp for killing crawlers bt Tripwire thought that adding a fire resistance for crawlers was smart. It wasn't.
- The teleportation system is a complete wreck, sirens spawning everywhere with no break isn't fair at all and can make solo players feel like they are playing Hell On Earth when they are just playing on normal.
- Even though the weapons are greatly animated there is a complete lack of them, only 4 specific ones for a class.
While I may still play it, it still shows that Tripwire have no intention of finishing the game anytime soon. If you liked KF1 then you may get some pleasure out of this game, but expect likable updates to be few and far between. This game has unimaginable potential the effort from Tripwire is not being put forth.

Early Access Watcher Reviews Killing Floor 2
Update Version: 1035
Disclosure: I played this during the free weekend starting on June 16th, 2016
It is a rare occurrence for me to find an Early Access game that turns the issues I normally find upside down. Usually EA games have poor optimization, terrible glitches and absurd loading issues, but this time around I managed to get a somewhat working product. I say somewhat very casually though. There are plenty of issues to come of this Tripwire assembly and not all are game related. Generally I try to inform of a game's status without mentioning politics, but due to the problems afflicting customers who have been backing this game for awhile, it might be a good idea to mention it. I will put this as a disclaimer though: their product is what caused me to not recommend Killing Floor 2.
The first thing most people will notice is the upgraded visual quality from the original Killing Floor. Lighting is much more distinct, weapon and landscape textures are greatly polished, shadow quality has more definition when interacting with flashlights and gore left behind from weapon shots looks great. Character models could use some more work, but enemy models are a leap ahead from the original in terms of refinement. The soundtrack is rather fitting with several high volume metal tracks promoting the horror setting without feeling overpowering. Sound effects from weapon fire, player grunts and enemy screams provide proper feedback. It all works in the game's favor and compliment the core gameplay people know and love.
The horde mode style gameplay has made a return from the original along with the class buffs and group mechanics still intact. The gist surrounds a group of six players fighting off waves of zombified horrors on rather small maps while building up a better arsenal to use against tougher enemies. The matches are always topped off with a boss fight from one of a few boss characters. There is a PvP style mode now as well, but due to the way the enemies are coded it feels lacking and sometimes underwhelming. The core gameplay is still the same from the original and extremely enjoyable in short bouts.
Some rather prominent design choices, which have been debated heavily by the community, have left the game feeling one sided and the charm of the original is faintly felt because of it. Zombies are granted the ability to teleport in this game when not on screen, which makes the barricade system of the original useless. It removes the strategy of enclosing enemies and funneling through certain locations and instead makes it a mob rush with very little teamwork or coordination. It also makes enemies appear out of thin air, creating hectic and sporadic combat that can leave one feeling battle fatigued by the end of a single match. Resistance was also added to the game and turned monsters into bullet sponges with certain weapons, leaving certain classes left out in the cold when it comes to weapon selection. This is just another example of trading strategic value for masses difficulty that makes it feel more like Left 4 Dead or End Times: Vermintide than the old Killing Floor people grew to love.
Even though the game has some passable optimization, there are some issues I found in regard to loading. Launching the game has resorted in five to ten minute freezes before the game arrives to the main menu. Other times it just decided to not execute at all, causing me to have to restart the game after quitting the process in Task Manager. Matchmaking is a headache with it endlessly cycling in search of a game when there are hundreds of empty games in the server list section. It makes using the search list the only reliable choice. These can be very frustrating problems, but nothing compared to the following issue: communication.
I reflected on this addition to the review for awhile and remembered the main point to early access was to allow constructive criticism from the community to make the game better. Tripwire has been on a major crusade to silence opposition on the forums in regards to feedback and anyone criticizing them for certain choices. Meaningful updates are scarce, promised game features are still nowhere to be seen, business practices equate to silence and when questioned on the release date, six months behind mind you, there is only silence. I am a firm believer in leaving the politics out of reviews, but in Early Access you are meant to release a product in a orderly manner with the aid of the community. This is not a demon hunt; investors have a right to be heard or at least understood, not ignored or deleted.
Micro-transactions are primarily stuck to cosmetics (special weapons and characters rewarded for owning other games aside), but Tripwire have been pushing the crates and $2.50 keys while neglecting key bug fixes and balancing. It is the use of micro-transactions in a paid game that make this problematic, especially in an early access game with PvE coding that needs to be addressed (enemies walking past you with no one around for example). This falls back to the silencing of critics on their business model which seems to be more concerned about randomized crafting and crates when a simple cash shop would have done. You are in early access to make games, Tripwire, not establish addition revenue sources when it forces you to extend deadlines.
I never would have written this review if the game didn't allow me to test it out for free. I am glad to see other players taking a stand against the lackluster development cycles and poor choices of Early Access developers. I urge people to keep treating these reviews as just that: a review. Potential is not what a game like this should be relying on, but rather its' own merit. The community that tests the game on different builds and machine hardware will have the insight needed to fix and improve. Ignoring that is not how this game improves. It could still be great, but at the current time it is very doubtful and with the scarcity of the updates I cannot recommend this game. Hopefully in six months this game will be free again for a weekend so I can re-review it, because I will not be purchasing it unless I absolutely need too.
Pros
- Gorgeous looking game
- Soundtrack is fitting with some good rifts
- Gameplay works and can be enjoyable in short bursts
Cons
- Micro-Transactions
- Developers censoring discussion on improving the game/business practices
- Design choices (teleporting, resistance, small maps) are 50/50
- Loading freezes, matchmaking issues

RISK OF PAIN would suit the title of the game a bit more, because at the start you expect it to be one of those run 'n gun games where you are a badass comando tearing everything apart without dying until the last few levels. But it's not! It requires patience and skill, and if played on Monsoon (the hardest difficulty) also prediction of every move of the enemy is a must to survive, because you die pretty quickly so you must act wisely, and not rush into the mob.
A few words about the game itself:
The game features 12 (if I recall correctly) characters, each with its own set of 4 skills. They all have very different play styles, so you probably will find one that suits your way of playing.
You start on a level and your objective is to locate the teleporter, which is always at a different location due to the random generation of item positions. On the way to the teleporter you battle enemies, collect items, gain experience, and at the end you battle a boss before entering the teleporter. Also with time the difficulty raises, so don't expect to overpower the enemies much too soon. So after getting to the last level you have a choice to enter the final level and beat the boss or you can continue to play on the previous levels but with increased difficulty, which ensures hours of replay value (My personal longest run was about 4 hours before I got bored and went to the final stage to get over with it already xD).
There are arround 150 items to unlock and pickup, each with a unique effect that improves your character. And the vast selection enables you to make your own combos that suit your character and play style after you've unlocked the artifact that makes items no longer random, but instead lets you choose which one from a specific tier you wish to obtain.
Also about artifacts. They are collectable items that can be turned on in the character selection screen once obtained to drastically change gameplay. They are scattered arround maps, usually at some hard to reach areas requiring you to have some mobility items already to successfully obtain them, others on the other hand require you to solve some puzzles.
Pros:
-great replay value
-lots of unlockables
-much customisable variation in terms of gameplay (characters, items, artifacts)
-local or internet co-op
Cons:
Theres only one con regarding the game itself in my opinion, and that's the fact that theres no server list or quick way to join a random internet game, but it still has that oldschool type of multiplayer where you just have two options, and those are either "Host" or "Join IP". So you are kinda forced to play singleplayer unless you know someone that has the game and is willing to play with you a.k.a friends (what I appearently don't have :( )
Conclussion:
Buy it, play it, cry about it, repeat!

It might sound like a backhanded compliment to call something "The Best South Park Game", but it's probably something South Park Studios would gladly slap on the box of this thing with all the underhandedness that that would entail, so we'll run with that. It's relevant that it's actually the best South Park game by a massive, orders-of-magnitude margin and actually manages to be a halfway decent game in its own right.
The plot revolves around your character, the New Kid, moving into a vacant house in South Park with your mom and dad. Within short order you stumble across the kids from the show who are fully wrapped up in a 4th grade LARPing session revolving around the Stick of Truth. You're quickly enlisted to help in the conflict between the Humans, led by Cartman, versus the Jewish Elves led by Kyle.
If you saw the "Console Wars" episodes of the show, they lead directly into this game in a way I don't think I've actually seen a licensed product do before. It's legitimately worth streaming them online prior to playing the game, as the game could really be considered just an extension of that plotline.
It's also a fun contrast to see what happens when the writers of the show aren't bound by Comedy Central's standards and practices. South Park as a show is known for pushing the envelope pretty seriously. South Park the movie had something like 250 uses of the word "♥♥♥♥", was obscenely violent, had Satan in a gay relationship with a (then still alive) Saddam Husein, and featured a giant talking clitoris onscreen as a plot macguffin.
The game puts the movie to absolute shame in terms of pure raunch.
This is easily the most gleefully offensive South Park has ever gotten, and they have things in this game the MPAA would've balked at. Were this a film it would've quite easily landed an NC-17 rating. I don't even want to spoil any of it because it's been a really long time since I've been genuinely shocked by a game, and this game managed to pull it off several times over the course of its 15 hours or so. Just by way of a comparatively mild example: You get "summmon" items in the game in a nod to Final Fantasy's summon mechanic, but here it's assorted bit characters from the show. One of them is Mr. Slave, who pulls his pants down and lands♥♥♥♥♥first on your enemies before stuffing them inside of him while he moans with pleasure (in my case he performed this move against a 4th grade hall monitor, which means I've played a game where an adult stuffs a child up his♥♥♥♥♥as an attack. Try to imagine if they'd put that in a movie, even as a joke.)
Get ready for a lot of cartoon nudity, basically.
It's not all sex jokes, either. The plot starts as a bunch of 4th graders playing live action Dungeons and Dragons but things dramatically escalate from there and the stakes become much more real-world and cheerily violent and dark, even as the game (very amusingly) never loses sight of the fact that you're just some 12 year old kid playing pretend.
This is used to attach a lot of legitimate RPG mechanics onto the game as well.You're given the ability to customize your character's appearance, though not their gender -- you're always male. To be fair the game does give a perfectly sensible plot reason for this and it's played up for humor later. You can find and equip new gear as well as "Materia" of a sort (here called "Weapon Strap-Ons" because of course) and as the game progresses you get a series of spells that can be used outside of combat for environmental challenges, like using your "Dragonshout" power (which is a fart, naturally) to ignite open flames and light anything behind them on fire to clear a path.
Bosses include the denizens of a meth lab, red headed hall monitors, goth kids, 16 year old girls, drunk hobos, assorted wildlife, nazi zombie cattle, aborted fetuses, and in one memorable instance your father's swinging scrotum which you have to dodge using a quicktime event.
Somehow it all actually holds together in the gameplay department. Part of this is due to the game being made by Obsidian who know their way around an RPG and have a good sense of how to interweave gameplay and narrative. The game's pacing is almost weirdly solid, even as it sticks to the fundamentals. There's a definitive first, second, and third act; sub quests are handed out at an even clip; you're given a narrative break after major plot events in the form of the day ending. It has the usual South Park problem where they never seem quite sure how to end the thing and it winds up getting so ridiculous that when it finally wraps everything up it kind of just...Stops, anticlimactically (which the game promptly lampshades and mocks, so).
On the downside, the game is really easy, to the point where combat actually gets kind of boring because some of the crew's powers are so overbearingly good. You're allowed to use an item at every turn before attacking; there's an item (coffee) that allows you to attack twice. If you're willing to just stock up on coffee and pound it every round for the difficult-ish fights they become snore-inducingly easy even on Hardcore difficulty. If you want challenge out of this you sort of have to make it yourself, because you almost have to try if you want to lose.
It also means that while there's a good amount of variety to the jokes, just because of the nature of turn-based RPG games you're going to start eventually hearing a lot of the same lines over and over again. Attack animations also cannot be skipped or disabled, which gets old quick as the really good ones come with comensurately lengthy animations attached to them.
It's stuff that probably could've been ironed out if the game had a little more time in the oven, but if you've read about the very troubled history of the development of this game it's actually pretty wild that it turned out as good as it did, where I have to scrape a bit if I want to find things to complain about.
Basically, it's short but it's reasonably mechanically solid, well voice acted, looks exactly like the show, and is honestly pretty funny and worth playing for the jaw-dropping level of objectionable content they managed to cram into basically every section of the game on what seems to have been a dare. Needless to say if you're easily offended or like to consider yourself above relentlessly juvenile humor because you worry deeply about what others will think about your values system instead of, say, reviewing the game in a public place so everyone will know you played and enjoyed it despite said objectionable content, then you should probably not bother with this game at all. If the idea of jokes about abortion, nazis, pedophiles, Canada, things that can be found inside Mr. Slave's colon (condoms, puppets, live bats, a working flashlight, an iPhone, etc.) and so forth doesn't sound like your cup of tea, your enjoyment of this game will probably be somewhat limited.

Batman: Arkham Knight is a dense and enthralling action-adventure game with a winding, if predictable, story that does make you feel like the Batman both inside and outside the Batmobile. There are too many Batmobile gameplay segments, however, making this predominantly similar in theme to that Batmobile-focused Batman arcade game. This is unfortunate, as the presence of the Batmobile ensured a much larger, multi-layered Gotham City that looks wonderful and was crafted with an unnecessary level of detail. The combat and stealth are the same as before, but their adjustments and brevity keep the familiar Batman sections just different enough to feel new. As intended, the Batmobile is a nice change of pace, even if its numerous sections get old and nearly overstay their welcome. From start to finish, there is constantly something interesting to take in and someone interesting to take down, making Batman: Arkham Knight in the end a game worth playing.

This game is leaps and bounds better than it's predecessors (especially the pile of slag that is Arkham Origins) in practically every way, aside from perhaps the uniqueness in atmosphere that Arkham Asylum had (being the first one and all). This game had a much less "rogues gallery" approach to the Batman Arkham franchise. Rather than moving from one boss fight from a somewhat related villain to another, the plot was much more focused around Scarecrow, the Arkham Knight, and
. Though for the most part a plot involving a previously defeated villain coming back for revenge is generally boring and overdone, they did an excellant job at flushing out Scarecrow as a great villain in his own right instead of just being one of the rogues like in the previous games.
In regards to the actual gameplay it was top notch, felt as smooth and crisp as the revamped combat for Arkham City, though of course with a few new moves and gadgets. Speaking of gadgets, I suppose I should mention one of the key gameplay mechanic additions to this game the Batmobile, or as I am going to refer to it as the Batmotank. A lot of people (used in the vaguest sense of the phrase) seemed to not enjoy the Batmotank portions of the game. Personally I found them rather enjoyable, both the high speed chase portions and the tank combat/sneak sections. They were different and used sparingly enough that it actually made the game proceed at a better pace for me. Instead of being alternating predator/combat rooms there was now some vehicle combat sprinkled in.
The only real issues that come about in this game was the post game content (or side game but basically things other than the main storyline). As most of the other villains involved 3-5 missions that were short and rather uneventful. Furthermore there was just so. many. damn. riddler puzzles, with the vast majority of them being collectothony. But at least the Riddler had a larger role than just acting as a green secret collect side quest culminating in actually a rather enjoyable boss battle.
In final notes, all I can really say is that this game was really well done, and probably one of the most enjoyable gaming experiences I've had in recent memory if not my gaming lifetime. Plus, super serious spoilers here, but
Overall rating 10/10

I highly recommend the Long War Mod for this game. There are several youtube videos on how to mod it , actually the LWM for Enemy Within is available on the Nexus and has it's own loader. But you should still watch a youtube video on how to mod it. There is also another program that is like a mod manager. It's called the XCOM UPK patcher Or UPK utilities also availble on the Nexus. It takes the mods that you download from the Nexus , which are in text form because these mods actually change the games core .ini files which is basically what this game is made of, and patches it with new parameters. The problem is unlike Nexus Mod Manager for Skyrim or Fallout 3, 4 , you cannot disable the mods from the UPK patcher. Once you add or change something , you have to track down what it is exactly that you changed or added and that is no small thing. So if you use it , use it carefully and by that I mean back up the original core .ini files before you use the UPK utilities patcher so if you don't like what you changed or added you can go back to the way it was.

I've never been a fan of strategy games on the PC. The turn based ones just aren't very good on this platform, whilst the RTS genre boils down to who can micromanage their units faster, in a powergaming orgy of 9.67 clicks a second. I'm a potato, not an octopus with jackhammer fingers.
If like me, you enjoyed things like advance wars and were born without the gift of being Asian, you'll find this game amazing, it's exactly what I've always been looking for.. Instead of using your brain to compute the fastest possible clicking pattern to achieve perfect micromanagement, everything here is down to planning.
You have 120 seconds in multiplayer, and forever in the campaign to manage your squad of six, and this squad of yours will get smaller very fast if you don't take your time.
Should you decide to buy this game (which happens to be a very good idea), I would recommend you do that in a retail store, or on your country's version of ebay. I got my copy for 19$ when it was triple that on steam.
And make sure you either play on Classic difficulty, or Normal difficulty with the Ironman setting. Don't be a sissy

If you're looking forward to the Batmobile, sometimes it's really fun and feels bad♥♥♥♥♥ Sometimes it controls like♥♥♥♥♥out of nowhere with no real explanation and it loves to wrestle the camera away from you while you drive.

Some of the game is a little TOO clunky to be excusable. There are too many sections where it's not entirely obvious what you're even supposed to do. I would wonder if I needed gadgets, or I had to go do something else, but it was generally just "even though you've followed the assassin's blood trail all the way here and it's entirely obvious whose it is, you need to go back and follow it again with your evidene scanner on" or, just as annoying, "you're not seeing how to progress because it's a grapple point at a weird angle above you that you have to be standing in an overlerly specific spot for before we'll let you use it, even WHEN you see it."
And I'll just point this out again: the game still crashes pretty commonly. Not enough to totally impede gameplay, but it ruined my immersion and will to play this more than once. Twice the crashes were even bad enough that I had to restart my computer just to get it usable again. They aren't why I'm fed up, but they're also there and VERY annoying. Here's to hoping that, by some miracle, more of this gets fixed. I love Batman and generally, the Arkham series. I know I don't want to bother trying to start from scratch now, though.

This is the best Game of the Series.
Let's adress the elephant in the room right away... Performance.
Does it run better after the re-realease? Yes! A lot better... but still only acceptable. It's definitely in a playable state tho.
The FPS in the game ranges from 10-20 in "over the city views" (which are very rare) to stable 55-60 on foot and during fights. Batmobil drops the FPS a bit (45-55).. apart from some occasional drops it's fairly stable. I'm playing on Normal Graphics settings with Gameworks turned off.
My PC doesn't even pass the "recommended" settings, so i would say it's pretty okay. However - the fact that other triple A games run much better on my PC is the reason for my "acceptable performance" statement.
Another thing you should prepare for are crashes. They seem to occur more often the further you progress.
I had about 10-15 crahes in total during my playtrough while most of them were during solving Riddles for the 100% completion.
I was about 75% into the Story when i had my first crash. The rest of them was during mentioned 100% completion which you need if you wanna see the ending.
----
Now that we are done with this, let's start with the review of the actual game.
Graphics are gorgeous, the story is one of the best of the series, batmobil feels like a batmobil should feel like.
The combat is more fluent and responsive than ever (excluding the Red Hood DLC more about that later).
Only the Environmental takedowns and the "knock guy with shield down" doesn't seem to work sometimes.
Locking the "real" Ending behind a 100% (or 120%) completion may seem annoying at first but makes sense. This is the last game of the series and if you follow the story you will understand why. Just make sure to be bring a lot of patience with you - especially when you are about to solve all of the 243 Riddles.. yes.. 243! Took me 3 days.
The DLCs for Batman (the extra 20%) are nice, introduce some known villians and can really be seen as fan-service for the fans of the Arkham series.
The Arkham Episodes (playing as different character e.g. Batgirl, Harley, Red Hood etc.) are sadly a bit too short. Most of them can be done in about 15-30 minutes. The only longer on is Batgirl which takes about an hour.
The Red Hood DLCs introduces some nice new combat moves and style but seems to be a bit clunky. Sometimes Red Hood was just standing there for 1-2 seconds after a takedown or special move not letting me control him while being beaten to death. Apart from that just another load of Fan-service for DC and Arkham lovers.
Overall i would say it's a recommended purchase. You get loads of content, especially if you like to collect stuff..
The performance issues are mostly fixed at least to an acceptable and playable state.
DLC and Arkham Episodes are just awesome.
