They really have fixed this game on a technical standpoint. I play at a solid 90fps on a evga gtx970 sc. Temps go to 75degC (I am here in Australia and ambients are around 35degC, i.e. very hot).  I have everything on the highest settings and all options enabled apart from the gameworks smoke because I don't like how it looks. My fps stay above 70 according to the steam fps counter, and I rarely (but not 'never') have stuttering. I also use GSync on a 144Hz monitor, so the fact that it remains above 60fps constantly means it runs butter smooth.
The cutscenes drop to 30fps, and with my eyes being accustomed to the over 60fps gameplay it is really jarring.
From a story point of view, I love it. One thing rocksteady does well is their story. Music, game mechanics and shear story writing all take my emotions on a run, and I really feel the stress, anxiety and helplessness at times. It really does its story telling in an exceptional fashion. I personally love the end they give to this saga. It really ties up the Rocksteady imagining of Batman.
The game looks absolutely stunning. Playing this game and then returning to other games in the series is incredibly telling on how far this game pushes the story. Batman looks awesome, the animations are fluid, the lighting is incredible and the reflections add a depth to the immersion that really is incredible. Going into photo-mode while gliding in the rain, and orbiting around Batman while the droplets remained stationary really took my breath away.
I really recomend this game. With over 120hrs on it I have really received my money's worth. It is unfortunate the game was released in such a horrible fashion. I was dissapointed with Rocksteady. It really was unacceptable. Due to that, this game will never really recieve the attention it deserves as it is right now. But in some ways, while the game doesn't deserve it, Rocksteady as a company does deserve to have consequences placed on them. I would rather they have delayed the PC launch than the ♥♥♥♥-up they released. Hopefully they will learn their lesson. This game is amazing as it is now, mostly because it's a finished game and not a ♥♥♥♥ed up beta version with massive technical issues.
I would recommend you buy this game.

Some initial caveats that may affect your game experience: I played this game on Classic difficulty, I focused on research more than outfitting my troops, and I neglected to build satellite nexus' - a fatal rookie mistake, well until later in the game. With that said XCOM is a fantastic game. The trade offs over what your area of focus is left me questioning decisions I had made well into the campaign. The enemies were brutal, well armed, and deadly accurate. I was comparatively weak, the constant underdog. But the climb, the work put into each facet of my facilities, and the well knit team I had crafted, all paid off. This game is exceedingly well made, the balances that the player strikes, paired with the work involved are what makes it exceptional. The tactics genre, the most frustrating of gameplay styles, does not overstay its welcome, instead it is well paced and fair in its gameplay. And even minor details are great. I still remember with some glee the faces of the captured aliens, worthy payoffs to the hectic process involved in their capture. Overall this game would rate for me the best of 2012, if not one of my favorite games of all time. It is well worth the purchase.

This game feels like the show. That's one of the first things I want to stress. The problem with alot of games based on movies or shows is they feel like a game that just has a loosely based wrapping of the thing they are based on (including previous South Park videogames). The Stick of Truth however... you feel like you're involved with the real show universe. The artwork, the plot, the humor and absurdity and complete disreguard of political correctness... it's all the same way the show would come across.
You basically play as the new kid that just arrived in town and get quickly swept up in this pretend medival humans-vs-elves game the South Park cast of kids are playing in a real life setting. Like all the kids in town. That pretty much remains a theme throughout the game. I don't really want to detail much about the story though since SPOILERS and all.
The combat in this game is more interactive than most RPG style games. It's turn based but you don't just select "attack" and select a target. In this game just about every move requires some interaction - usually clicking at the right time to make a hit land.
Seriously if you like South Park the show then you'll like this game!

Imagine going to an arcade, and finding one of those quick action games where you need near impossible reflexes to win a butt munch load of tickets, that just drains away your supply of quarters and tokens. and then you rage because you didn't win squat.
Now imagine if you didn't have to use quarters or tokens, yet play the same thing. Enter super hexagon. Its a rather simple arcade-style game. You guide a small little triangle around a hexagon, while making sure you don't get squished by the advancing walls of doom. sounds easy, no?
THIS GAME IS HARD. BE WARNED.
this game will make you rage at one point or another. But heres the thing. its totally doable, unlike some arcade games. Sure, you need reflexes of the flash, but its totally possible to be a hyper hexagonest master. besides, all you need to do is survive 60 seconds in each stage (Hexagon, hexagoner, hexagonest, Hyper hexagon, hyper hexagoner, and hyper hexagonest). so in theory, you could beat this game in less that 7 or 8 minutes, including menu time.
but that won't happen, in most cases.
Anyways, while the price is a bit steep (unless you got it via holiday sale, then good for you), the game is worth experiencing, if not for the rage, but for the sheer enjoyment for when you beat it. Also, I must mention the good music.
Also, if someone ever made an arcade game of this, which was coin op, I tell you it would be a bestseller right off the bat. xD

Today just won a Deity level game for the first time...had won on hardest level on all previous versions of Civ but this time it took me quite a long while.  This game is much HARDER then the others!
SUGGESTIONS
Tailor your play style to the Civ that has the bonuses you play to.  I usually play defensive, with lots of diplomacy, so I played a diplomatic Civ for my Deity win.  Remember that you aggressors out there have a harder time with Conquest Victory, Civ 5 is not conquest friendly, as it takes much more effort to capture an opposing city.
Play for points!  Don't let opportunities to score points pass you by even if they do not fit into your over all scheme!
Do not get discouraged if you're losing in the opening era's.  You can make it up later if you have a solid plan.  I was behind the whole game on my Deity win and still pulled out the victory!
Plan ahead!  If you absolutely have to have a certain Wonder to win, then make that your priority!
Religion is not to be underestimated.  You can score serious points without much effort, should you found your own.
War is not the end-all and be-all of victory.  I just won on Deity level without waging a single war.
Espionage WILL get you back in the science game.  Just let it play out, and do not get discouraged!
Overall, this game, in my view, is the best of ALL the Civ's, dating back to the first.  As I said, I played ALL versions of this game, and this is by far the best.  The options a player has far surpasses the old "death stack to win" Civ games, you actually have to think this game through, and plan ahead.  In that regard, it's more chess, then checkers!

It's pure arcade madness, using your twitch reflexes and playing "in the zone" like you were dancing through a bullet-hell type game. Just when you think you have done well by passing through a level, the next one introduces an even bigger challenge. With perseverance, the results start to get better, little by little.
Why buy the game? I found an actual reason to play the game. It's a great warmup and training method for concentration and reflexes. If you play any competitive game you'll need the same sort of concentration you can get by going through Super Hexagon. I play about 5-10 minutes to wake the eyes up a bit, that's all it really needs. Another way I've used it is to just play with actively trying to concentrate, using everything I have to make better results. That's more of a stamina type training that gets longer as you get used to it. Maybe you get one good result and after that a series of really bad ones -- Don't worry, that's part of the training, soldier. Gotta keep that concentration up all the time, shutting out all those errant thoughts. In that sense it resembles meditation training somewhat.
Would someone play this for fun? I don't know, it sounds a bit weird. You need to have some sort of competitive edge if you want to enjoy Super Hexagon, or at least a wish to perform better than you did yesterday.

Since performance has been the most prevelant issue for the game, my review will focus on that.
I preordered this game months before it came out. Why would I do something so stupid? Because it was announced that the game would have LInux/SteamOS support, and I wanted to show support for my primary but otherwise niche platform. This support was finally cancelled a few days ago. I was going to get a refund, but I decided to look at recent benchmarks to see if all the performance issues I had heard about in the PC released had been fixed. It looked like my i7 5960x and Titan X were more than enough to handle the game.
At 1440p, with maxed out settings (except for debris and smoke disabled, those are to Arhkam Knight what Hairworks is to The Witcher 3), during the game's performance test as well as the actual gameplay my framerate is typically in the 80's and occasionally in the 70's. In fact, I get more performance than with The Witcher 3 on the same hardware. Although The Witcher 3 does look a bit better (with Arkham Knight being my 2nd best looking game).
I decided to try it on my laptop with  i7 6820HK and a GTX 980m and a 1080p gsync screen. In the performance test and in gameplay with maxed settings (except debris and smoke), I have never had lower than 60 fps.
I think given the visual fidelity of the game, it's not unreasonable for a game to require some decent hardware. Sure the game runs on ps4... but it runs at 30 fps and is a jagged mess (but still worth it if it's your only option). The PC version has more detail, and (probably) a higher draw distance. I think if a little gtx 980m can handle this game without a stutter at 1080p and fulls settings, performance is probably in pretty good shape. (take this with a grain of salt, but I think the GTX 980m is supposed to have the performance of a GTX 970)
That being said, this game had no business being released on PC in the initial broken state that it was in.
To be fair, my desktop has 64GB memory and my laptop has 32GB memory and Arkham Knight is installed on to high end SSD's on both systems, so I can't comment on whether or not the paging issues have been fixed for the game. (If you're curious, the reason I have so much memory is because on occasion I need to run a lot of concurrent virtual machines for testing relating to my work)

An amazing game, a must buy, a must play, if you have enough money to buy it then just buy it now.
Best way to buy it is through the Orange Box, not just do you get Half-LIfe 2 but also Episode One and Two, plus portal.
An action packed game with great moments such as entering the Citadel and getting the Super-Charged Zero Point Energy Field Manipulator, or dashing through Ravenholm.
Earth in this time of story has been taken over by Combine forces, but Half-Life isn't one to tell you the story uphand, that can be found with uncovering the deeper story.
No time for cut-scences, well there aren't any but that's okay as it keeps you being the Gordon Freeman, it realy does imerse you in the game. Not just comat based based but also Physics too, with some here and there small Physcis puzzles. Later in the game as you progress, gather more weapons and more harder Combine enemies hunt you down you can take control of Antlion insects (something that was once an anoying enemy) and members of the Resistance (People like you who are trying take back Earth and their lives).
Throwing and shooting explosive barrels is aways fun.
Weapons of Crowbar and Gravity Gun, Glock and Magnum, SMG and Pulse Riffle (both have alt shots), Shotgun and Crossbow, and Grenades and RPG.
There are two veichles in which you'll encounter in the game, the Boat and Buggy, personally I never liked the Boat and Water Hazard is one of my least liked chapters in the game, but the Buggy is pretty cool.
There are boss battles (if you would call them that) from Hunter-Choppers, Gunships, Striders and Antlion Guards. Over coming these challanges is always an amazing thrill. Each place is always destinctively different and fun.
The main problem I have with this game is that even with all this action, a lot of it at times felt a bit samey, but that is dealt with costant upgrade of tools and weapons. Another fault with the game (Both are fixed in Episode One and Two) is that you never seem to stay in one place, always constantly moving from a-b and no c, even though places are memerable.

A must have, a must buy. Make sure you also get Episode One and Two (they are expansions), and best way to buy is through the Orange Box.

It was pretty good. Not my GOTY, but I think it would be in my top 10 of 2015. Now, before you crucify me, just hear me out, alright? Put the gun down... HEY, PUT THE DAMN GUN DOW...
STORY: You are Bruce Wayne, AKA Batman. After the death of The Joker in Arkham City nine months post-Arkham City, crime rates have declined in Gotham and it seems that things are normal. However, The Scarecrow threatens to unleash his fear toxin upon Gotham, causing the city to evacuate and for Batman to get back into his suit and go after him and restore peace to Arkham for possibly the last time. However, a militia lead by the Arkham Knight, a villian who nobody knows anything about, has teamed up with Scarecrow, causing things to be more difficult than they would usually be. The story is alright, it isn't as good as it was in City IMHO, but it was better than Origins.
GAMEPLAY: Combat is refined, it feels better than it did before. Stealth is there, and it feels more viable. Still, it feels awesome to beat thugs up, and while that still is an option, it is a bit harder of one than before. There's a new FEAR takedown system, which lets you take out up to three thugs (five with upgrades) before you go into combat. There are medics now who revive enemies you knocked out and give existing enemies a boost, take those out ASAP or else it will be harder to deal with. The usual thugs from the last games are there, too. Boss battles are fine, nothing as awesome as the Mr. Freeze battle, but it's fine.
We also have the Batmobile now, and let me tell you... eh, it's alright. It isn't as awesome as I wanted it to be, it feels a bit lighter than it should have been, but at the same time, I don't get where people are coming from when they say it's terrible. It's pretty fun, and I liked using it.
GRAPHICS, PERFORMANCE, AND LEVEL DESIGN: Okay, let me say this first and foreforth: I don't know if anyone else will have better luck with a different rig. That said, I had no issues at all. None. I think that all of the issues are fixed as far as I can tell. Graphically it looks amazing too. And don't go all "But dog, it looks better on PS4, nyeh!" SHUT UP! It still looks good. So shut up. Gotham looks good, it has a lot of details to it, all three islands are nice to be around. The open world looks nice, there are a lot of cool places to explore, and I can't complain
CHARACTERS, VOICE ACTING, AND DESIGN: Batman is voiced by Kevin Conroy like the last couple times, and he does a good job. Scarecrow is played by one of the guys from Fringe, he's spooky as hell and is the best voice actor in this whole thing. The Joker also kinda has a role in this, and Mark Hamill still kicks♥♥♥♥♥ Other than that... well, it's kind of weird. I mean, the voice acting is top notch, but it seems kinda emotionless. Kinda hard to explain. Character design still looks good, no complaints there.
SIDE ACTIVITIES: You're Batman, you got a lot to do. Save firemen, save Catwoman from the Riddler, ♥♥♥♥ around with the Arkham Knight's militia's stuff. Some are better than others of course, I get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off at the thought of doing the Riddler trophies and challenges, but ah well. There are also the AR Challenges that you can play, if you're into those, you can play them.
FINAL VERDICT: I don't blame you if you're still a bit butthurt about the performance issues day 1, but it shouldn't cloud your judgement of this game. 8/10, if you like the Arkham games, or are a big Batman fan, it's now $40 off sale, I grabbed it when it was $24. If not, maybe wait for a future sale where it's off more.

Sid Meier's Civilization V is an amazing game, a definition of the genre that would make you crave for more. You build cities, research technologies, explore the world, meet other people and try to win in an unforgiving world where your allies might suddenly backstab you and your centuries old nemesis could suddenly be your best friend. Do you try to act passive and maintain relationships with your friends, or you risk breaking alliances and do what is best for your people? Do you go for short term victory or play the long con?
As your people rise from club-bearing savages to upstanding citizens, you find new ways to run things better, but everything comes at a cost. Want to improve your defenses? Then you need to hold back on the infrastructure. Want to build a wonder to awe your people and reap the benefits? Then you need to make sure it's worth the time and risk the very real possibility of someone else building it first and your hard work converted to a few bits of coin, a worthless consolation.
With over 40 civilizations to choose from, randomly generated maps (which you can tweak to your liking!), support for mods and absolutely great gameplay, Sid Meier's Civilization V would capture you and hold you hostage as you convince yourself: "Just one more turn..."
Pros:
- Very high replayability
- Supports mods
- Easy on the hardware, for last resort you can even play with 2D graphics called Strategic View, might even run on a toaster
Cons:
- As with games of this genre, sessions can be slow and generally consume a lot of time
- If you play too frequently, things might get samey after a while, took me about 100 hours to get a bit bored, but that's happens to everything.
- Multiplayer with mods is a bit spotty
- As with games of this genre, expansions change the gameplay by quite a lot, and there are civilizations and maps that are only available in packs. Thankfully the Complete Edition (which indeed comes with every DLC available for the game) goes on quite often.

Any content updates are few and far between ever since this game's release in April of 2015.  Since then there's only 2 bosses to fight in survival mode.  They're both nothing special and are bullet spongey.
The progression system where each class can be leveled to a maximum of 25, takes an incredible sum of time and each perk gained after every 5 levels are not very unique (ie. more dmg/reload quicker etc.).  Might I suggest going to a custom map called "Perktraining" if you really want to grind out experience points.
I lost interest in the recent PVP mode, quickly.  If you join in midway through a game you cannot jump right in and will have to wait until the end of the round.
I found that many of the original maps are flat and not very interesting.  I eventually sought custom maps, regularly.
I wouldn't recommend this game unless it's heavily discounted.  I plan to try this game again at its full retail release in the Fall of 2016.

It took a while, but Tripwire's gotten their thumbs out and brought the game to a pretty fun level. Listening to the community has worked well, here's some of the really good things they've done:
* The resistances have been scaled back an insane amount, so they're actually subtle. Just about any weapon is effective against the zeds.
* Perk skills have been dialed way up to have a more pronounced effect, there's few skills that feel like filler and most can drastically alter a playstyle. Medic's probably the biggest change which has worked out for the best.
* Drops are daily, not weekly, now you tear your hair out over crates way less.
* Teleporting isn't an issue anymore, no more zeds popping into existance via hate and line of sight
However, there's still some things that need to be fixed:
* Firebug got brought to a good level, then nerfed again which is annoying.
* There are still filler skills that no one will take since they serve almost no purpose (Medic Poison), which could be reworked or buffed
* Weapons that flat out never get used due to lack of strengths, Firebug Trenchgun was my favorite weapon in KF1 but now it's pretty rubbish. No zerker takes the eviscerator, and the firebug's microwave gun rarely sees use now.
* A subjective thing, but Rae's design bugs me. I made Tom Banner my liege immediately, the original characters have personality and the retro characters were awesome. Some woman sprinting around in a rockabilly dress with open heel shoes though, really? The voice acting's good but the character doesn't look like she's a survivor dealing with legions of zeds, she looks like she's stumbled out of a production of Grease. For everyone that wanted another cool female character she must have come as a shock.

Nov 8: They've fixed some bugs, but not all of them. I have beaten the game once, and I enjoy it a good amount, but there are some glaring problems here that keep me from being a full supporter of it.
The game is actually really fun when you're playing with a friend, blasting through stages and collecting items and blowing enemies up. The difficulty is just right, and the enemies don't seem to get totally overwhelming. When solo, though, the game is entirely different, and becomes a strange suicide rush to try to get as far as you can. It's actually really infuriating, because there isn't much you can do when you roll a bunch of bad items in a row. I just finished a run where all twelve items I got were utterly useless to the point that I might as well have not picked them up at all. In contrast, I've had runs where I get three nice items to start with and suddenly I'm facerolling through everything for awhile.
The game is seemingly balanced around you either having a buddy to play with, or having access to an item called the Command Artifact that actually lets you choose what items you want when you open a chest. Unlocking Command involves getting a few stages in, hoping it rolls a certain one, and grabbing it, so it can be a pain to unlock.
I'm enjoying my time with this game, and I definitely expect to get some more hours out of it, but I can't say that I think it is a good purchase. The game has been totally bugged for a few weels, and the first batch of fixes they released feels more like a band-aid than a cure. The game kind of forces you to play co-op, or die repeatedly until you get lucky enough to get a good batch of items in order to unlock the Command Artifact in order to actually play the game as seemingly intended.
Dec 14:
I have pulled 23 hours out of the game now, and I honestly feel like I won't be returning much more, if at all. Over one month of owning it, and weird bugs still persist. Co-op, at the moment, is totally broken, despite working a few weeks ago. The jumping bug is fixed, where you would lose the ability to jump when you landed at the apex of your jump (the game thought you were still in the air due to the lack of downward momentum) but now there appears to be a lotto-like crash-to-desktop that only happens upon killing the last boss.... which means you can play for awhile, go to finish it off, and then suddenly learn that all the work you just did was fruitless.
Beyond those bugs, though, the game is just far too random for my tastes, and if I equip the artifact that lets me choose my items, the only thing I have to hope for is that I don't have a string of chests spawning in bad locations, and then I end up trivializing the entire game after a few minutes. I mean, it's a fun game. Out of my 23 hours, maybe five of them were purely unenjoyable... but that's five hours too much, and now when I play I'm either insanely frustrated with awful chest locations or I'm steamrolling through everything.
I got it for free, so I can't complain much, but this is also one of my longest reviews, and one of my only negative reviews, so, I guess I've complained a lot. Either way, expect anywhere between five to 25 hours of fun, and at least a couple of hours of pure frustration.

I have played this game for far longer than Steam says. I had a version from GOG, but when I bought the latest Humble Bundle and got 4 copies of Risk of Rain, I decided to bring the game here and switch my save file over.
Risk of Rain is a simple 2d platforming game. You spawn at a random location on the map, have to locate the teleporter, kill enemies, kill bosses, collect items. Very simple idea that works to become a very addicting game that you'll find yourself playing over and over even after you unlocked most items and characters, because it draws you in, beckoning you to keep playing, to try to make that Origin Artifact run, to see if you can survive on Spite, to try and bea the game as that one class you're pretty awful at.
The game has a simple 'philsophy' I guess you would call it. The longer you play, the harder it gets. And that actually happens. At the top-right of your game you'll see a timer and a bar, with the bar filling up as time increases. As time increases, your difficulty increases, going from very easy at the start to HAHAHAHA difficulty around 25-40 minutes into the game, depending on if you're playing on Monsoon (hard) or Rainstorm (normal). Don't play on Drizzle. Drizzle is for cowards. There are also artifacts that can increase the difficulty if you find yourself bored of normal mode. Glass artifact increases the damage you do by 500%, but you only have 10% of your normal HP, meaning one hit can kill you at the start. Honor artifact makes it so the enemies that spawn are all elite, meaning you'll always be fighting enemies that can fire red rockets at you as you run, enemies that emit an aura of healing to everyone (except you) around them, or enemies that can shock you to death if you stay too close. Spite is very simple: As enemies die, "funballs" are released, meaning small circle items that will explode after a time, with larger enemies releasing more funballs, so if you're in a closed area and fighting a Parent, you're dead.
The game has 12 characters to unlock as of this writing, but you only start with one: Commando. Each character has a somewhat unique playstyle so you'll be able to find your favorite quickly as you play. Commando is the fast-shooting, rolling, "normal" guy of the group, since all of his abilities are somewhat, well, normal. Bandit is your button-spammer who fires faster if you press the button faster, as well as having other cowboy-like abilities like aiming headhots or throwing dynamite. Miner is a melee character who is all about using your i-frames (invincibility frames) to get in close to the enemy and wreck them with your charges and drill shots. The new patch added Loader and CHEF, but I won't talk about them. They're great, but no spoilers for you.
The game claims to have 100+ items for players to collect and use. If you use the Command artifact, though, that number is gonna be greatly cut down because you're just going to stack certain items. A few of the items are also "Use" items, meaning you need to press a button to use them, and you can only have one of them at a time. White, green, and red items, however, can be collected and stacked as you please, so you can wear 6 rings and inject 8 stringes into your body. The latest patch added new items, and again, some are good, some you don't really need. Hint: Get as many hopoo feathers as you can. Jump for the stars, kid.
Sadly, the latest patch did bring with it many problems/bugs that can kill your enjoyment in some ways, like the latest bug (as of this writing) that makes your skills, HP, and XP bar disappear if you die in a multiplayer game and revive in the next level. However, the game is still great fun and I recommend it to anyone that wants something to play with their friends. And if you do want to play it with your friends? Go buy it off the Humble Bundle, you can get 4 copies of it right now. Yes, right now. Go get it. Now.

I guess that the only thing that could've mitigated the "PR nightmare" this game has would've been a disclaimer that says: "Game was designed to run in 30 FPS".
Technical issues review:
At least on NVIDIA cards, this game runs really well on 30 FPS with adaptive framerate or capped at 30 fps. 60 FPS gives you a slew of game inconsistencies on the framerate that is more than likely related to it being produced at 30 fps.
Now, if you do play this game at 30 fps with the recommended specs on most stuff on normal quality settings, it runs solid.
To max out the graphics you need at least 6 GB NVidia graphics preferably a GTX 980 or 980 Ti, and even then you might want to play the game at 30 FPS. If you're not OK with playing at that frame rate, just don't bother and skip. Just as a note, the game runs for me on a 3770 with 16 GB of ram and a GTX 960 with everything on high with adaptive vsync and the FPS set to 30fps like a champ, it never dips below 30 fps, but that's with no anti-aliasing enabled and NVidia exclusive effects off.
Game itself:
This was a very well-produced game (in terms of story writing and presentation), and perhaps it has the most movie-like feeling of all of the batman games. It's a step above the previous one, and the game is an action oriented game at heart. If you liked the more adventure-collection based games of the first two batman games, I advise you skip it.
All in all, a steal at half price, with a healthy dose of free DLC.

Ok, so I was waiting for 9 month to make a positive review. As you see, i can neither wait, nor make it positive. Why? Well, here it comes:
1) EA is not really a good one. Rare additions to the game, rare bug fixes, rare balance fixes (and that sometimes makes a perk totally useless till next patch, for month). Even when a content patch comes, it may be not what everyone asked for.
2) The damage system. Protip: if you have a working formula, dont change it. But who would listen? So with current patch zeds are so much harder to kill, that I found it hard to beat a map on hard with 25 lvl perk ( i could solo suicidal while drinking tea before that "new awesome resistance system"). Why does anyone need harder mods when all the zeds have their effective HP doubled?
3) VS mod. The reason I have the second point on this list. Not only noone needed it, but on release it appeared, that the game is balanced to kill waves of zeds, not for zeds to counter and kill survivors in a PVP mod. So what do we do? Add some new features? Nah, just buff all the zeds. All the games I saw in VS mod ended on wave 2. Nice balancing, tripwire.
4) Microtransactions. In early access game. That does not have even half the content they promised (well, on its release at least). Yes, it is cosmetic, yes, I dont use it cause I dont want to. But dont you dare to say that system coded itself and skins drew themselves. It all consumes time that could be spent, i dont know, on what they promised to do year ago.
5) Perks. I thought that KF1 was a bit slow on progress, but at least each lvl made you really stronger. lvl 6 perk was better than 2 lvl 0-s (in terms of game impact). Now you have 25 lvls, 5 of which matter (cause they give you perks) and the rest is just to fill the gap. You dont even feel 1% of damage increase per level, and some perks aren't really that great (so true with the last update). So not only progression feels slower now, it also doen't feel like making much of a difference, max and min levels are still kinda feelable, but anywhere in between does not give you any satisfaction. And in MP games if someone checks your lvl, they check 5 "perk milestones", so you can safely say that the game has 5 perk lvls against 6 in the first KF.
6) Highly subjective, but as for me, with current bullets any zed can eat, all the weapons feel like they are made of bread and shoot butter. Tripwire is famous for their great gunplay, but this one is really below their standarts. Also, 1 weapon per tier with 4 tiers - it is not even remotely enough. I get it, kf1 had most of its weapons added after in patches, updates and DLCs, but you are not really making a first game in series, you set yourself a level, try to perfom on it.
Well, that is all for now. For now, cause the game is not even out yet and I already have several serious issues with it. And  they might not even finish it in a year (better make more useless features noone asked for). I will update review when new patches show up, but with current gameplay I am not going to bother playing it (and I dont recomend you bothering yourself).

In Dead Space, you play as Isaac Clarke, an engineer part of a repair crew sent to the USG Ishimura, a large space ship that has ceased communications. However, apart from a routine comm repair job, the crew finds the ship derelict without a soul on board, and its halls covered in blood.
Dead Space is a third person shooter of the survival-horror genre, and a fantastic game. It gets a lot of things right, the foremost of which are its masterfully crafted atmosphere and engaging narrative. The atmosphere, created from great use of lighting and sound, really provides immersion and suspense as you make your way through the dark corridors of the ship.
The story is cliched, but is done so well that that doesn't matter. Its engaging nonetheless, and is told by not just the plot events, but the entire game, from the menus to the environment.
Definitely recommended if you enjoy third person shooters, immersive games, or survival horror.
This game is extremely addictive, with a great soundtrack and almost no cost. Recommended for all of those who likes speed and mental challenges.

The game works fine, and with friends it can be a blast, but be cautious before purchasing Killing Floor 2.
The devs continue to implement features nobody asked for, yet constantly blame time constraints for delays regarding perks and new maps. Adding a fully realized micro-transaction cosmetic item shop before the game even left EA brings to question Tripwire's ability to manage funds. Especially considering the price of this game when it initially came to early access.
The maps are each great but other than a couple strongly lack variety. They follow a similar circuitous setup.
The zeds are faithful to the first game and the viscera system is amazing. The way the creatures fall apart is helped by how well the guns handle. At first the gameplay handled well but as new perks and a more recent “resistance” system for the zeds have been implemented the balance is completely out of whack. Some perks are no longer worth using and others (Demolition) have been underpowered since release.
Given that the game has gotten worse as it gains MORE content, it does not bode well for the future of this title.
All my grievances aside, the game is technically competent. It controls well on both keyboard and controller, and if you have friends to play it with you can have a great time. I advise not to purchase at full price; wait for one of the numerous free weekends that are provided by Tripwire.

Ok, so I was waiting for 9 month to make a positive review. As you see, i can neither wait, nor make it positive. Why? Well, here it comes:
1) EA is not really a good one. Rare additions to the game, rare bug fixes, rare balance fixes (and that sometimes makes a perk totally useless till next patch, for month). Even when a content patch comes, it may be not what everyone asked for.
2) The damage system. Protip: if you have a working formula, dont change it. But who would listen? So with current patch zeds are so much harder to kill, that I found it hard to beat a map on hard with 25 lvl perk ( i could solo suicidal while drinking tea before that "new awesome resistance system"). Why does anyone need harder mods when all the zeds have their effective HP doubled?
3) VS mod. The reason I have the second point on this list. Not only noone needed it, but on release it appeared, that the game is balanced to kill waves of zeds, not for zeds to counter and kill survivors in a PVP mod. So what do we do? Add some new features? Nah, just buff all the zeds. All the games I saw in VS mod ended on wave 2. Nice balancing, tripwire.
4) Microtransactions. In early access game. That does not have even half the content they promised (well, on its release at least). Yes, it is cosmetic, yes, I dont use it cause I dont want to. But dont you dare to say that system coded itself and skins drew themselves. It all consumes time that could be spent, i dont know, on what they promised to do year ago.
5) Perks. I thought that KF1 was a bit slow on progress, but at least each lvl made you really stronger. lvl 6 perk was better than 2 lvl 0-s (in terms of game impact). Now you have 25 lvls, 5 of which matter (cause they give you perks) and the rest is just to fill the gap. You dont even feel 1% of damage increase per level, and some perks aren't really that great (so true with the last update). So not only progression feels slower now, it also doen't feel like making much of a difference, max and min levels are still kinda feelable, but anywhere in between does not give you any satisfaction. And in MP games if someone checks your lvl, they check 5 "perk milestones", so you can safely say that the game has 5 perk lvls against 6 in the first KF.
6) Highly subjective, but as for me, with current bullets any zed can eat, all the weapons feel like they are made of bread and shoot butter. Tripwire is famous for their great gunplay, but this one is really below their standarts. Also, 1 weapon per tier with 4 tiers - it is not even remotely enough. I get it, kf1 had most of its weapons added after in patches, updates and DLCs, but you are not really making a first game in series, you set yourself a level, try to perfom on it.
Well, that is all for now. For now, cause the game is not even out yet and I already have several serious issues with it. And  they might not even finish it in a year (better make more useless features noone asked for). I will update review when new patches show up, but with current gameplay I am not going to bother playing it (and I dont recomend you bothering yourself).

The game works fine, and with friends it can be a blast, but be cautious before purchasing Killing Floor 2.
The devs continue to implement features nobody asked for, yet constantly blame time constraints for delays regarding perks and new maps. Adding a fully realized micro-transaction cosmetic item shop before the game even left EA brings to question Tripwire's ability to manage funds. Especially considering the price of this game when it initially came to early access.
The maps are each great but other than a couple strongly lack variety. They follow a similar circuitous setup.
The zeds are faithful to the first game and the viscera system is amazing. The way the creatures fall apart is helped by how well the guns handle. At first the gameplay handled well but as new perks and a more recent “resistance” system for the zeds have been implemented the balance is completely out of whack. Some perks are no longer worth using and others (Demolition) have been underpowered since release.
Given that the game has gotten worse as it gains MORE content, it does not bode well for the future of this title.
All my grievances aside, the game is technically competent. It controls well on both keyboard and controller, and if you have friends to play it with you can have a great time. I advise not to purchase at full price; wait for one of the numerous free weekends that are provided by Tripwire.

Killing Floor 2 is a great game if you enjoy co-op shooters, with up to six friends.
Pros:
- Solid gameplay: Don't listen to the others saying the game sucks because its missing stuff. The stuff its missing is 2 more perks which will come, and more maps, which again will come with time. This being said the game already has a good map selection and 8 perks to pick from.
- Eight Perks/Classes: regardless of people complaining about how long it will take the make the new perks, etc. Remember this game is still in developement don't ♥♥♥♥♥ so much just wait. On top of that there is now more perks in killing floor 2 than the original.
- Leveling is pretty quick in my opinion, especially compared to the first.
Neutral:
- Maps:  They feel a little small to me, but that's coming from someone who played the original. The maps to are in decent amount of #, and more are to come as they game is still in development and there's a steam workshop as well.
- The cosmetic items are ONLY COSMETIC. They have impact on gameplay, especially the character cosmetics as its a first person shooter. The only cosmetics, if you decide they're worth buying, would be the gun skins as you can actually look at it while playing
- Updates are a bit slow and some what far inbetween, but when they do update they are typically massive updates. Normally adding maps, balancing, and a new perk.
- There is a weapon and a few characters that are blocked off unless you own other games. Again characters are cosmetic mostly ( only mostly as they all have different quotes) and the weapon can be shared/unlocked for play if one of the players in the lobby owns the game.
- Bosses: The bosses scale, along with all the other enemies, to become harder both by increased health and damage output based on the amount of players. The bosses themselves, as of now there are two, can be quite a pain the♥♥♥♥♥if you're playing with a lot of players who LACK cordination. Otherwise they're fine. I only mention this as several have complained about them being too difficult.
Cons:
- (This complaint is only because I'm comparing it to the orignal). Several of the perks in game feel off, mostly the firebug, berserker, and support specialist.
- Competitive Mode: this is a personal preference. The gamemode isn't very fun to me and i feel like the player sirens could use a nerf.
Overall if you're looking fun a coperative wave-based survival game this is a good one. Personally i prefer the original. If you buy the upgraded version of this you get both killing floor 2 and the original killing floor.

Long and the short of it (TL;DR): Good game. Solid game play. Enjoyable. Can be difficult at times (lol). Not an FPS. Optional soldier voices, kill cam, etc. If you're a die hard x-com fan that believes this is blasphemy: don't play this game. Cause you'll never enjoy it. Let the rest of us enjoy this little gem.
While I didn't play too many of the original X-Com games, I did play the first one. This is no direct replacement for the old one, and definitely doesn't have the deep micromanagement that X-Com:UFO Defense had. What it does have are smaller squads (Think more like a kill team/seal team six) with abilities to round them out. It gives more meaning to individual soldiers and utilizing their abilities against a larger alien force. Imagine storming an alien battleship with six elite soldiers (if you're doing it right) armed with the proper gear and class abilities to work together as a cohesive group.
Another thing which I was worried about was map size. Welp, definitely not worried after doing my first playthrough (Classic difficulty, Ironman). The larger maps are rediclously huge, which makes me happy there were not as many soldiers being ordered about as it would take a long time to get done.
If you're looking for a remake, look to Xenonaughts (closer to a reskin and remake in an earlier time period, and which will be finished...sometime). If you're looking for one of the better X-COM games that is more a reimagining (and from what I understand comes closer to what Gallop wanted in the game) then give this a shot. The Demo doesn't do it justice, look for a sale or find a friend who'll let you give it a whirl. It is still a difficult game (Hell, I had to start over/quit and start a new game 10x because I made a tactical error or made a poor tactical decision, etc.) So don't go in thinking it'll be a cake walk.
Most importantly, if you do grab it. Have fun. :)

This game is pretty awesome. It's like Resident Evil 4 (with better controls) mixed with System Shock mixed with Event Horizon. Your mileage may vary on whether it's scary or not, but it's definitely scarier than the later installments. The story is nothing to write home about and you can probably see one of the major plot twists coming a mile away. This doesn't prevent it from being an enjoyable game though.
What DOES prevent it from being a 100% enjoyable game is the fact that it has 'console port' written all over it. The FOV is fairly low as you might expect. There are also quite a few mouse problems, including mouse acceleration that cannot be disabled, lower vertical sensitivity than horizontal, and sensitivity that varies wildly based on your frame rate. Additionally, the in-game Vsync setting is completely ♥♥♥♥ing broken. It locks you to 30 fps and introduces an unplayable amount of input lag.
If you have a computer capable of running the game at a consistent 60+ fps (which isn't difficult) I would recommend forcing on Vsync and triple-buffering in your graphics card driver if you have an AMD card or using D3DOverrider if you have an Nvidia card. This will fix the inconsistent sensitivity. If you have a mouse that lets you adjust the DPI separately for each axis you can set the Y axis DPI higher than the X axis DPI to compensate for the Y axis being less sensitive. There's no way I know of to remove the acceleration. The FOV can be increased using Widescreen Fixer but it will make menus farther away from the camera and thus more difficult to read, so you may have to toggle it off periodically.
Other than the technical issues I think Dead Space is still a great game and I would definitely recommend it.

This is an OUTSTANDING Arkham game, but it comes with a very big IF...
...If you can run it without issues. I was one of the lucky ones, I guess, as I was able to play the game on my system (MSi Dominator Pro GT60 2pe w/ 8GB Geforce GTX880M and 24GB RAM) from day one and did not have any of the issues that others had (though I did have to turn off the smoke physics and debris physics to get playable framerates). A lot of people did not have such luck, and so this game has rightly got a lot of negativity.
But, if it does run well enough on your machine, then you are in for a treat, because this is a great continuation and completion of the Arkham games saga. Batman still batmans like a BATMAN! BECAUSE HE'S BATMAN! The fighting is just as smooth and excellent as it was in Arkham City (and lacks whatever tweaks ruined the flow in Arkham Origins), the Batmobile, while overused, is a lot of fun. The story is great. The side missions are great. The Riddler stuff is tedious, but that's kind of expected at this point, and it has a pretty good pay-off in terms of the satisfaction of beating that jerk. ;)
So, yeah, I am recommending this game, but with that huge caveat: it may not run well on your system, and so you may end up having wasted your money. Only buy this if it is at a price point at which you don't feel it would be a waste if your machine can't handle it now (and don't buy it all if you don't ever expect to have a machine that can play it well). Or maybe consider getting the console version (though if you are like me, you may prefer playing Arkham games with kb/m) which is at least guaranteed to run.
But, if you do get it, and it does run on your machine, then you are in for a treat. :)

You have to keep rhythm really well. The barriers fly around rapidly, changing types very often and requiring different modes of attack. But you have no time to think, and you can't pause the game, so be on the ready!
It took me a while but I beat the first mode, Hexagon. You need to pass 60 seconds in a mode to beat it. A recommendation: Use your mouse buttons, not the keyboard. I can't say about a controller, as I haven't tried. Further, turn off VSYNC.
In any case, a fun game that is equally frustrating, but I can't fault it really. It is what it is.

XCOM loved by a mass of old school gamers and peeking interest in the new ones.
Firaxis pulled this reimagining of fairly well, it retains the tension of the originals. The management of upgrades and soldiers, the feeling of losing a Team leader in the heat of a Sectopod ambush.
The gameplay is exciting and balanced, the UI is not perfect but a large improvement from many of the previous variants and originals. It does what it set out to do extremely well.
The downside is while it's gotten a lot of things right, towards the end of the campaign you unlock some abilties (if your team members haven't been slaughtered) which you don't often have a lot of time to play with unless you've purposely stopped progressing just to knock down random UFOs.  The game also has a feeling it could be more open, more activities a slightly more involved air to air system and the like.
Overall XCOM: ENEMY UNKNOWN, is essentially the feeling of you watching someone get their jimmies rustled, then waking up and realizing it was you.

The Early Access felt boring and lacking compared to KF1, I suppose for the obvious reason of it being in Early Access, now after two years the game has enough perks, maps and weapons to actually feel like a Killing Floor game.
Interestingly Tripwire moved from the KF1 model of releasing new guns, characters and skins in DLC packs, which amounted to £96.79 worth of content on top of the base game, to a CSGO-esque model. Where "CSGO-esque" means they almost copied the exact system; I guess Valve showed there's money to be made in an RNG based system with an absurd Marketplace economy. But at least this time it only seems to be skins, emotes, etc. that are locked behind a key and crate so personally I'd say it's probably better.
The ability to not only change your character but to also customise the head, body and other accessories is a welcome addition to the game in my book. As is the new perk leveling system; instead of an "up to level 6 system" where if you weren't level 6 you didn't have a decent starting weapon and most people would just kick you from the session you now get an perk relevant weapon from level 1 and up to level 25 you gain extra bonus eg. resistance to damage sources and increased weapon damage. Also, every 5 levels, per perk, you can choose one of two 'skills,' these skills allow you change/upgrade a lot of your mechanics/stats - again furthering your ability to customise in the game, this being the most significant though as it allows you to upgrade stats that suit your playstyle, directly affecting your game.
The music is also great, as expected from Killing Floor.

At first glance this may seem like yet another franchised game, made by a nameless developer for some quick cash. This is a franchised game and if you don't care for the franchise in question there's no need to waste your time reading on.
However, if you're neutral, open minded, or undecided; then you should be aware the game studio that developed this title, Obsidian Entertainment, have a number of well-respected games to their name, and the developers that comprise it have had involvement with some of the most acclaimed WRPGs - I'm talking: Fallout, Planescape: Torment,  Baldur's Gate, Icewindale, Arcanum, Neverwinter Nights, KOTOR 2, Fallout: New Vegas, and now: South Park: The Stick of Truth.
For the South Fans, this game was scripted and voiced by Matt Stone and Trey Parker, who I believe were heavily involved in the development of the game; if you think the show is funny, chances are the humour will tickle you once or twice. The cut scenes are suitably melodramatic (think imaginationland special) with appropriately outlandish scenarios, complete with many and varied references to the show.
As for the gameplay: the combat is turn-based and features various time-based, button mashing and button combination techniques, which is why I actually play this with a console controller. I have tried the game with keyboard and mouse, and I've not really been into consoles since the Dreamcast, but I find the controller much more satisfying (not to mention intuitive, little doubt this game was made with consoles in mind) and I can sit on the sofa while playing it. The thief was my class of choice; the skills require the least button bashing and are more rhythm based (also, bleeding is great).
The world is a dungeon crawl of the streets of South Park, enterting peoples houses for loot ad repeatedly can get a little old but this is for the explorers and completionists only; feel free to go straight to the main quests. My major complaint is how easy the combat can be with the right weapons and use of potions. This is only compounded by being restored to full-health and power points after each battle; something that would be unthinkable in the more hard-core RPG Baldur's Gate 2, which was challenging to the point of rage induced euphoria with certain mods. However, this game is about emphasising fun: the combat is fun despite being easy and the plot is lightheartedly offensive.

(This is mostly just me getting most of my frustrations off my chest with this game, so it might sound a little biased. Sorry but I need to rant. Feel free to skip if you don't wanna see that.)
Yes the game is extremely buggy and I'm sure you've heard all about that, that does suck, and did indeed hinder a bit of my experience (even though I found myself being able to work through most of the bugs alright with some tweaking and paitence) But I think that even if the game had been working at it's full capacity, it still would have still been quite a letdown.
The combat and stealth mechanics in the game are alright, the same as it has always been albeit now with some additions thrown in the make it a bit tougher (which it didn't really, even on the higher settings), but they tend to really screw the pooch with the addition of the Batmobile. I personally didn't mind it so much when you used it for driving around, racing and solving puzzles, but of course they had to keep adding on and on to the utter boredom instilled by the constant tank sections. These wouldn't be so bad if they just used it for a level or two (three at maximum) but it's just so shoehorned into the game that it becomes unbearable. I might be exaggerating a bit, but I'm under the given impression that the tank fighting took up more than half of the game and it got so utterly dull that I didn't come back to this game for months after starting. But that's just adding something stupid and unnessesarry onto a pretty decent formula that the games have been following for years and years now, so that's gotta look pretty minor in comparison when the rest of what we know has gotta be good right? Wrong. Some of the most basic things that are important to the formula are so screwed up that I find it baffling. Maybe they were just so focused on fitting in that stupid bat-tank that they thought we wouldn't notice. Well I noticed and quite frankly I am annoyed. First off the boss fights in this game are awful, utterly dreadful, they're almost nonexistant. There are so many different villains thrown into this game, that you would think that at least one would have a boss fight worth a damn. Even the ones in Arkham Origins were better. At the very least they tried to add something, this game just took it away. I could understand if they just wanted to keep the boss fights to the main story considering the amount of stuff in the game, but out of all the different times where they could fit in an awesome boss fight, they decide to just implement a cutscene instead (including one very frustrating instance where you should get to fight a giant robot). There are only a few things in this game that I could call boss fights, and they all sucked. They were either slightly more difficult stealth sections, more stupid tank stuff, and a lame goon that took slightly longer than usual. I won't pretend that the boss fights in the other games were the greatest things ever, but I can at least say that they could be fun (most noteably that Mr Freeze thing from Arkham City, that may be one of my favorite boss battles of all time.) and memmorable. There's not even a boss fight at the end of the game against the main villain, what is with that?
Oh and speaking of the villain, I suppose I should talk about the story. For the most part it's a joke. It tries to build mystery and suspense, but mostly fails as I found things to be so utterly predictable. I could see so many twists and turns coming from a mile away, and the main villain barley appears throughout the main game, it's ridiculous. The self proclaimed Arkham Knight that they named the game after, was just downright boring and whiney. I was tempted to put him on mute for most of the game. And his identity revalation had me ranting for days on end about just how stupid it was for a number of reasons, either because it's just a poorly done retread of a classic batman story, or by the fact that they didn't think to do anything new or interesting with him.
The only saving grace I can think of for the story in this game is the addition of one particular character from the previous game who keeps popping up all throughout the game. That character and their interaction with Batman was the thing that made me want to finally finish up the game, it was marvelous. Shame they couldn't fit anymore of that into the game.
Generally I consider this game tedious and mediocre with some fun sequences thrown in from time to time. I don't think i'm ever gonna be able to replay this, and I have a pretty good record with replaying games, even if I thought that they were just alright.

XCOM: Enemy Unknown is the first computer game I have played in over a decade, and it has been addictively fun! The variety of strategies involved in combat and research adds a great deal of replay value. In addition, the cool graphics, camera angles, unit customizations and difficulty levels make each playthough feel challenging. In spite of the number of glitches and graphic errors I would still highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a really unique gaming experience.
_________________________________
XCOM: Enemy Within adds a new dimension of replay value to XCOM:EU, with the addition of MEC units, gene modifications, new alien threats, enemy factions, maps, missions, weapons and Second Wave options.  This is not simply another DLC, but an Expansion in the truest sense of the word.  Enemy Within literally expands the boundaries of the XCOM universe, giving players much more variety and choices in protecting the earth from invasion.  The inclusion of MELD has significantly changed how to approach strategic combat.  No longer can you creep along, hunkering down behind cover until you uncover aliens.  Players learn to adapt a more aggressive approach, in order to recover the much needed resource to augment your soldiers for Genetic Modification or as MEC troopers.  This makes for a much faster gameplay on the battlefield.  Difficulty has also increased significantly on “Classic” and “Impossible”, providing a greater challenge for veteran players.  Like the original XCOM, this game also has its share of “bugs” primarily with crashing and freezing on the load screen.  However, in spite of this, XCOM: Enemy Within is such a profound addition that fans of the game will find plenty to enjoy.

EDIT 2: TWI has done a complete 180 on the game. Resistances are pretty much gone, the classes are more powerful than ever, and the game is in the best state it's been since it was first released on Early Access. I'm keeping the review for archival purposes (but changing the recommendation to Yes instead of No), but it no longer applies to the game as of early September 2016.
EDIT: Tripwire has reversed some of the resistances, but not removed the stupid thing. It's more playable than before, but still not that fun. Plus, the team seems hell-bent on making the game more unfun and annoying to play, so I'm keeping this review up until Tripwire straightens up their act.
I do want to note that Tripwire is communicating with the community a bit more than before, but I want to see positive changes, not just fluff.
Let me say this straight: I loved the basics of Killing Floor 2's gameplay. The gore and gameplay are very satisfying and kept me playing for a long time. However, the latest update served as the straw that broke the camel's back and made me stop playing KF2 (at least for the time being). Here's why.
* A horrible, horrible resistance system that turns Killing Floor 2 into a 90s RPG, like Baldur's Gate. Firearm damage is now divided per weapon type, meaning that a bullet from an assault rifle can do more damage against one enemy, but do terrible damage to another. It makes no sense. Because of this, most classes are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ against most enemy types in a half-baked attempt at promoting class diversity, making most of the weapons unfun to use; a cardinal sin, since one of the game's key points is fun gunplay. In order to be effective, you have to read a goddamn spreadsheet to know exactly what weapons suck and what weapons work against each enemy type. I'm serious. This isn't the 90s; you shouldn't have to read a spreadsheet and memorize a bunch of variables just to shoot enemies in the head.
What's worse is that the resistances make no goddamn sense. A completely naked woman can take shotgun shots and explosions like a champ, but melts if she eats a handful of bullets fired only by an assault rifle. Meanwhile, a naked man on fire can tank nearly anything for no apparent reason. Fire I can understand because he's on fire, but damage from assault rifle rounds doing half damage? Really?
You can get used to the system, but the fact of the matter is that there's no reason why this system was considered a good idea and fun. If you want to encourage class diversity, make the classes kick♥♥♥♥♥in their own way (which, ironically, Tripwire was getting close to until the Sharpshooter update dropped) or maybe make enemies weak to certain weapon types, not resistant to most of them. Making enemies resistant to attacks from most weapons for the sake of encouraging teamplay is awful; all it does is turn enemies into unfun bullet sponges.
* The team blows off criticism they disagree with, which goes against the point of EA. Confront them about an issue, and they'll throw their feet down and say "BUT IT PLAYED WELL IN INTERNAL TESTING", as if a game being played by a handful of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s in a small office that can consult the devs is equal to it being played online by thousands, often with complete strangers. If you're going to be like that, just make it a full game instead of pretending the game is Early Access and listen to people.
*The Sharpshooter perk was delayed in favor of a PvP mode few wanted and that was essentially stillborn, despite promises that it will increase the playerbase more than a new perk would. It's poorly balanced and a mess to play to thanks human players being able to stomp human-controlled enemies, even with the Sharpshooter update revising it. Before the Sharpshooter update, PvP had one or two active servers at max. I expect it to go down to that level a week after the Sharpshooter is released.
* Terrible patching system. Most companies would patch major issues as they came up; not Tripwire! Tripwire often packs a ton of fixes into one giant package released every 4 or 5 months instead of issuing quick fixes.
One example is the auto-raging at the end of a wave; heavy hitters, like the Scrake, would automatically enter their rage mode (endless sprinting, mostly) when there were five or less enemies. There was no way to make them stop; if you didin't have enough people to deal with the enemy or a class that could handle him, the game was over right there with no chance to prevent this.
The kicker? It took Tripwire several months to fix this, despite complaints about it appearing a few days after the patch that added it went live. Why would a game-ending issue allowed to persist for several months except for incompetence?
* 1 step forward, three steps back when it comes to balancing. When Tripwire wants to nerf a class, they will nerf it into utter uselessness.
The Berserk perk became quite powerful after the Firebug and Demolitions update. When people complained about it, it took Tripwire almost a full year to "fix" it, even though opinion was divided if it was OP or not. When they did "fix" it, it was nerfed to the point where it's currently useless thanks to a terrible rework of the Berserk's skills and the awful resistance system making all of the Berserk's primary weapons do half or less damage to every foe.
I hate to post this review, because KF2 has solid and addicting core gameplay. However, Tripwire seems to have no idea on what direction to take the game, but seem hell-bent on making the game more obtuse to play for God knows why and ruining the core gameplay for the sake of making it hardcore or some crap like that.
If Tripwire pulls their asses out of their head like Overkill did, I'll come back and give this game a positive review. For now, I'm not playing this game and I'm keeping this review up.

This game in its current state is more than playable. I run an Intel i7 with 8 gigs of ram and a 4 gig GTX 960 and average around 55 FPS in 1080p on Win 7. There are some frame drops at certain times where a lot is going on but really not that big of a deal. The graphics are done with extreme detail even down to the assets. I understand the complaint from those who pre-ordered as I would not be happy either. Now I am not saying it is okay but we all make mistakes. Now to rate the game as a whole for what it is worth without a childish hop on the bandwagon review. I will talk about this game going forward for anyone who would like to purchase it.
The open world design grant a great backbone to this games development which also subsequently allows for DLC to be added into the game seamlessly. The vanilla "story" if you will is great with a twisted plot that any comic/batman fan should enjoy. You can attack many different scenarios in a way that suits your playing style. If your bored you can wander the streets like in a GTA game and cause havoc or in this case beat up some bad guys.
Now how does the game run. My GPU is NOT overclocked and I get 55+ FPS 90% of the time. I can only imagine a 970/980/TITAN to be way better. This is with all my settings maxed out on high with the exception of the nvidia interactive smoke, fog, rain, etc which is disabled. Now if you don't have a 900 series GPU or 4+ gigs VRAM this is where it might get tricky. I does use most of my VRAM. I don't have a 750 ti so I can't compare. As I don't know how it will run on 2 gigs VRAM or the older GPUs. It may be a struggle. I can say that anything above a 960 4GB shouldn't get a complaint.
I suggest every future reviewer leave your system specifications in the review so it can be judged for accuracy.

Now alot of people say that this might not be true considering "they dont know how to play" but have you ever actually looked at the stats of a lvl 25 medic and then compared them to a lvl 0 medic? In the end it makes a huge difference and I think if there is a versus mode or in general there should be an anti-cheat.
But instead of actually adding an anti-cheat (which 90% of the community probably disagrees with me because they use a trainer or perk servers) or finishing the game they added crates. Same system as on Csgo. Only difference is the playerbase does not put up with it meaning there was around 50.000 Players to begin with but since they added all the player crates there are only about 2.000 daily players left.
The Newest Maps that got released are also rather lazy made, it seems like they just copied alot from other maps then puzzled it together. Apparently those maps are not even made by Tripwire but by some other modders from the community they are just put in the game. There are by far better maps then those ones as they are very restricted and mostly a copy + paste job which is rather boring.

However, if you're neutral, open minded, or undecided; then you should be aware the game studio that developed this title, Obsidian Entertainment, have a number of well-respected games to their name, and the developers that comprise it have had involvement with some of the most acclaimed WRPGs - I'm talking: Fallout, Planescape: Torment,  Baldur's Gate, Icewindale, Arcanum, Neverwinter Nights, KOTOR 2, Fallout: New Vegas, and now: South Park: The Stick of Truth.
For the South Fans, this game was scripted and voiced by Matt Stone and Trey Parker, who I believe were heavily involved in the development of the game; if you think the show is funny, chances are the humour will tickle you once or twice. The cut scenes are suitably melodramatic (think imaginationland special) with appropriately outlandish scenarios, complete with many and varied references to the show.
As for the gameplay: the combat is turn-based and features various time-based, button mashing and button combination techniques, which is why I actually play this with a console controller. I have tried the game with keyboard and mouse, and I've not really been into consoles since the Dreamcast, but I find the controller much more satisfying (not to mention intuitive, little doubt this game was made with consoles in mind) and I can sit on the sofa while playing it. The thief was my class of choice; the skills require the least button bashing and are more rhythm based (also, bleeding is great).
The world is a dungeon crawl of the streets of South Park, enterting peoples houses for loot ad repeatedly can get a little old but this is for the explorers and completionists only; feel free to go straight to the main quests. My major complaint is how easy the combat can be with the right weapons and use of potions. This is only compounded by being restored to full-health and power points after each battle; something that would be unthinkable in the more hard-core RPG Baldur's Gate 2, which was challenging to the point of rage induced euphoria with certain mods. However, this game is about emphasising fun: the combat is fun despite being easy and the plot is lightheartedly offensive.
Pretty fun game, nothing revolutionary or particularly amazing, just an enjoyable way to waste time.

EDIT 2: TWI has done a complete 180 on the game. Resistances are pretty much gone, the classes are more powerful than ever, and the game is in the best state it's been since it was first released on Early Access. I'm keeping the review for archival purposes (but changing the recommendation to Yes instead of No), but it no longer applies to the game as of early September 2016.
EDIT: Tripwire has reversed some of the resistances, but not removed the stupid thing. It's more playable than before, but still not that fun. Plus, the team seems hell-bent on making the game more unfun and annoying to play, so I'm keeping this review up until Tripwire straightens up their act.
I do want to note that Tripwire is communicating with the community a bit more than before, but I want to see positive changes, not just fluff.
Let me say this straight: I loved the basics of Killing Floor 2's gameplay. The gore and gameplay are very satisfying and kept me playing for a long time. However, the latest update served as the straw that broke the camel's back and made me stop playing KF2 (at least for the time being). Here's why.
* A horrible, horrible resistance system that turns Killing Floor 2 into a 90s RPG, like Baldur's Gate. Firearm damage is now divided per weapon type, meaning that a bullet from an assault rifle can do more damage against one enemy, but do terrible damage to another. It makes no sense. Because of this, most classes are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ against most enemy types in a half-baked attempt at promoting class diversity, making most of the weapons unfun to use; a cardinal sin, since one of the game's key points is fun gunplay. In order to be effective, you have to read a goddamn spreadsheet to know exactly what weapons suck and what weapons work against each enemy type. I'm serious. This isn't the 90s; you shouldn't have to read a spreadsheet and memorize a bunch of variables just to shoot enemies in the head.
What's worse is that the resistances make no goddamn sense. A completely naked woman can take shotgun shots and explosions like a champ, but melts if she eats a handful of bullets fired only by an assault rifle. Meanwhile, a naked man on fire can tank nearly anything for no apparent reason. Fire I can understand because he's on fire, but damage from assault rifle rounds doing half damage? Really?
You can get used to the system, but the fact of the matter is that there's no reason why this system was considered a good idea and fun. If you want to encourage class diversity, make the classes kick♥♥♥♥♥in their own way (which, ironically, Tripwire was getting close to until the Sharpshooter update dropped) or maybe make enemies weak to certain weapon types, not resistant to most of them. Making enemies resistant to attacks from most weapons for the sake of encouraging teamplay is awful; all it does is turn enemies into unfun bullet sponges.
* The team blows off criticism they disagree with, which goes against the point of EA. Confront them about an issue, and they'll throw their feet down and say "BUT IT PLAYED WELL IN INTERNAL TESTING", as if a game being played by a handful of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s in a small office that can consult the devs is equal to it being played online by thousands, often with complete strangers. If you're going to be like that, just make it a full game instead of pretending the game is Early Access and listen to people.
*The Sharpshooter perk was delayed in favor of a PvP mode few wanted and that was essentially stillborn, despite promises that it will increase the playerbase more than a new perk would. It's poorly balanced and a mess to play to thanks human players being able to stomp human-controlled enemies, even with the Sharpshooter update revising it. Before the Sharpshooter update, PvP had one or two active servers at max. I expect it to go down to that level a week after the Sharpshooter is released.
* Terrible patching system. Most companies would patch major issues as they came up; not Tripwire! Tripwire often packs a ton of fixes into one giant package released every 4 or 5 months instead of issuing quick fixes.
One example is the auto-raging at the end of a wave; heavy hitters, like the Scrake, would automatically enter their rage mode (endless sprinting, mostly) when there were five or less enemies. There was no way to make them stop; if you didin't have enough people to deal with the enemy or a class that could handle him, the game was over right there with no chance to prevent this.
The kicker? It took Tripwire several months to fix this, despite complaints about it appearing a few days after the patch that added it went live. Why would a game-ending issue allowed to persist for several months except for incompetence?
* 1 step forward, three steps back when it comes to balancing. When Tripwire wants to nerf a class, they will nerf it into utter uselessness.
The Berserk perk became quite powerful after the Firebug and Demolitions update. When people complained about it, it took Tripwire almost a full year to "fix" it, even though opinion was divided if it was OP or not. When they did "fix" it, it was nerfed to the point where it's currently useless thanks to a terrible rework of the Berserk's skills and the awful resistance system making all of the Berserk's primary weapons do half or less damage to every foe.
I hate to post this review, because KF2 has solid and addicting core gameplay. However, Tripwire seems to have no idea on what direction to take the game, but seem hell-bent on making the game more obtuse to play for God knows why and ruining the core gameplay for the sake of making it hardcore or some crap like that.
If Tripwire pulls their asses out of their head like Overkill did, I'll come back and give this game a positive review. For now, I'm not playing this game and I'm keeping this review up.

A finger twitching, body sweating, seizure inducing, and crack-like addicting game that will make you wonder, "Why didn't I purchase this lovely game earlier?".
The game is set in the year 3045 and runs its course in an alternate one dimension universe. You play Peter Pointer, a spy for the CPD (Coalition of Pointer's Dominion). You have just completed your daily reconnaissance of the enemy, the IAHV (International Association of Hexagon Villains). Unfortunately, you were caught by the watchful eye of the hexagons and now you are running for your life. You must now evade the deadly touch of the encroaching hexagon security guards. Sounds easy right? WRONG! The hexagons have recruited backup: squares, and pentagons. 60 seconds secures your safety, but reaching that far is easier said than done.
Three keys are needed for this game: the left arrow key, the right arrow key, and the spacebar; you'll be needing the spacebar the most. In the options menu, you have the choice to turn vsync on or off. Personally I leave it off because it feels more responsive.
